stories.title: Haryanvi dancer accuses youths of attacking her car in UP:Performer says they break windows with sticks; calls it shameful behaviour
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary has alleged that she was attacked while travelling through the border area of Greater Noida and Bulandshahr in Uttar Pradesh. She claimed that two youths struck her car with a stick, damaging the front windshield before fleeing. A video of Dimple Chaudhary crying after the incident has also surfaced on social media. In the video, she says there is a limit to such shameless behaviour and claims she was on her way to her sister's house when the attack took place. She also shows the damaged windshield of her car while describing the incident. Dimple told Dainik Bhaskar in an interview- After the attack, I was very scared. I became unconscious, due to which I had to be taken to the hospital. I had received threats before, but the police did not take action. Now the police are waiting for a major accident. I will soon file a complaint with the police regarding this matter. Dimple said that on Monday, she was going with her younger brother to her younger sister's place in Sikandrabad, Bulandshahr. Around 11:30 PM, on the way, bike-borne attackers targeted her Brezza car. After the attack, both fled from the scene. SP Rural Antariksh Jain said - The entire incident was investigated. This case is not from Bulandshahr, but from the Alpha police station area of Greater Noida. Since it is a matter of the border area between Bulandshahr and Greater Noida, the singer was mistaken. Greater Noida police are investigating the matter. First, see the pictures- Unconscious due to fear, brother took her to the hospital Dimple said - The car was being driven by the driver. It stopped at a CNG pump on the way. Where my brother bought cold drinks and chips. During this time, I also received a call from a friend, so I was talking to her. The fatal attack happened around 11:30 PM. My brother and the driver took me from there to the hospital. After that, I did not go to my sister's house. I returned to my own home. Dimple alleged that during the attack on the car, I had neither any bodyguard nor any weapon in the car. In such a situation, the attackers could have killed them. Received death threats over the phone The dancer said - The last time I received a threat on the phone, I went to the police station and filed a complaint. There, the policeman talked to the accused on the phone, but I was made to sit at the station for about two hours. When nothing happened, I returned home. No action has been taken in that case yet, and now there has been a life-threatening attack. The caller had identified himself as the Don of Chambal On June 18, Dimple Chaudhary also received a threatening call. She said that the caller had identified himself as the Don of Chambal. The person threatening her said, "I will pick you up from your house. An AK-47 will come out of your house." She had shared 2 audio-videos related to this call on her social media account. First Recording Caller: Madam, I saw your reel. Dancer: The whole world watches reels, that doesn't mean you'll call me. Caller: I have fallen in love with you. Dancer: I will give you very bad abuses. You are misbehaving. Why do you use such words that force me to abuse or speak wrongly? Have you fallen in love in your old age? Where did you get my number? Caller: I will take out an AK-47 from your house. Dancer: Say that again, what were you saying? Caller - If you want to record, go ahead, no problem, okay. Dancer: What do you mean an AK-47 will be taken out of the house? Second Recording Dancer: Why are you bothering me? Caller: I will forcibly take you from your house. Dancer: How can you forcibly pick me up from my house like this? Caller: Am I a cannon and a dacoit from Chambal? Dancer: If you're from Chambal, how can you forcibly pick me up? Caller: I'll tell you how I can pick you up after I do... (swearing) If you record this, I'll *** you. Dancer: I didn't say anything to you. Nor am I recording you. There's no recording on an iPhone either. Caller: I have an iPhone too, are you thinking that only you have an iPhone? Dancer: I've never seen you, nor have I ever met you, so how did you fall in love with me? Caller: Do you want to record this and play it for the police? Tell them this is the don of Chambal. Dancer: I swear on my brother that I haven't made any recording?

stories.title: Bus' wheels detach at 100 kph, overturns thrice:Crashes through divider onto other side; passengers say driver was drowsy
stories.summary: A major road accident took place on the Agra–Delhi Highway on Wednesday morning, when a roadways bus running at around 100 kmph lost its two front wheels mid-journey. After this, the bus went out of control, overturned three times and then crashed into the divider. The entire roof of the bus was ripped off, and seats were torn out and scattered on the road. Meanwhile, panic broke out among passengers inside the bus. All passengers started screaming for help. Local passersby rushed to the spot and began rescuing people one by one. On receiving information, police reached the spot and admitted the injured to SN Medical College. Out of the 12 passengers on board, 10 were seriously injured. 3 pictures of the accident Passengers said - The driver was drowsy, driving fast Ambulances were used to shift 10 injured passengers to SN Medical College. After the accident, a traffic jam was created on the highway. The bus was later removed using a crane. The driver fled from the spot after the accident. Passengers told police that the driver, Lavi, was driving at very high speed. About 10 km before the accident, they had also warned him. The bus had narrowly escaped crashes at one or two places earlier as well, but the driver did not slow down and eventually the bus overturned. Bus conductor said - I was scared Injured bus conductor Rupendra said he only remembers the bus hitting the divider after which he lost consciousness. He said he was frightened and remained unconscious for about 1–2 minutes. When he regained consciousness, he saw that the bus had overturned. These passengers were injured The injured passengers include Dharam Singh, Chandravati, Rupendra, Lakshmi Devi, Jitendra, Kanhaiya, Arvind Kumar, Sachin, Shyamvati and Mohit, who were admitted to SN Medical College. The injured passengers belonged to Agra, Etawah, Khairagarh and Firozabad. Sikandra police station inspector Pradeep Tripathi said that there was no loss of life in the accident, but several passengers were injured. He confirmed that the front wheels of the bus came off, causing the bus to overturn and hit the divider.

stories.title: Electricity bills in UP set to reduce from July:Power companies collected ₹2,801 crore from consumers using incorrect fuel surcharge
stories.summary: Electricity companies have imposed a 10% Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) surcharge in June based on incorrect calculations. Over the past 14 months, the power companies have reportedly recovered ₹2,801 crore from consumers using the same faulty method, whereas as per rules they were allowed to recover only ₹684 crore. The regulatory commission has reprimanded the electricity companies and directed them to ensure correct calculation of FPPCA from July onwards. Electricity companies committed this kind of arbitrariness Electricity companies calculate FPPCA every month and recover it through bills. For example, the difference in electricity purchase rates in March is added to July bills as FPPCA. In June, a 10% FPPCA was charged, which was supposed to be calculated based on the price difference of electricity purchased in February. However, the electricity companies also added ₹1,400 crore of previous dues, leading to excessive recovery. Challenge was given in the commission The 10% FPPCA was challenged by the Consumers Council in the Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Regulatory Commission. The commission summoned the electricity companies. On 19 June, the companies submitted their calculation data and admitted that they had been using the same method for the past 14 months. It was revealed that the companies were adding previous outstanding amounts every month in FPPCA calculations. As a result, instead of recovering ₹684 crore, they had collected ₹2,801 crore. Preparation to collect 10% FPPCA in July as well Electricity companies were also preparing to levy 10% FPPCA in July, but the commission’s order has now stopped this. Only the actual difference amount can now be recovered. The commission has directed that from July onwards, FPPCA must be calculated correctly. Petition filed to recover excess collection On Wednesday, a new petition was filed in the UP Electricity Regulatory Commission by Consumers Council President Avdhesh Verma, demanding the refund or adjustment of nearly ₹2,200 crore excess charges collected in the last 14 months. The following demands were made through the petition Know what FPPAS is FPPAS (Fuel and Power Purchase Adjustment Surcharge) is an additional charge added to electricity bills when the cost of fuel used in power generation or electricity purchase increases, so that the extra cost can be recovered from consumers. The electricity department says the surcharge was imposed due to rising costs in power generation and procurement. It also mentions that fuel prices, including petroleum products, have increased amid global conditions. Consumer Council President said - Expensive electricity has broken the back When the 10% surcharge order was issued, the Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Consumer Council President Avdhesh Kumar Verma opposed it. He said that in February 2026, 10% fuel surcharge was already being recovered. At a time when people are facing severe heat, power crisis and inflation, increasing electricity rates would break the backbone of common consumers. He also claimed that the Electricity Regulatory Commission had approved electricity purchase cost at ₹4.94 per unit, but in March 2026, the Power Corporation showed electricity purchase at around ₹5.86 per unit, thereby imposing an additional burden of around ₹1,610 crore on consumers. He further demanded investigation into how and from which private companies such expensive electricity was purchased in March 2026, alleging that electricity was continuously being procured at higher rates from private producers. He also said that earlier claims of around ₹1,400 crore were also added in March FPPCA. Energy Minister AK Sharma had also expressed displeasure Energy Minister also expressed anger Uttar Pradesh Energy Minister AK Sharma also expressed displeasure over the fuel surcharge. In a review meeting in Lucknow, he wrote a letter to UPPCL Chairman Ashish Goel, stating that the working style was irresponsible and decisions were being taken that were bringing disrepute to the government. He said that a 10% surcharge was imposed without informing him, and its recovery also began in June bills. He further stated that such a major decision was taken without his approval, which led to negative publicity against the government in media and social media.

stories.title: Father shoots son dead in Fatehpur:Daughter-in-law shot in stomach while trying to save him; accused flees on bicycle when police arrive
stories.summary: In a shocking incident in Fatehpur on Wednesday, a father allegedly shot and killed his son and also fired at his daughter-in-law when she rushed in to save her husband. Hearing the gunshots, neighbours rushed into the house, by which time the accused father had fled from the spot. The injured couple was immediately taken to hospital, where the son succumbed during treatment. The daughter-in-law, who sustained a bullet injury in the stomach, was referred to Kanpur due to her critical condition. Police, on receiving information, recovered the licensed double-barrel gun used in the incident. The case is reported from Sitapur village under the Bindki police station area. See 2 pictures The incident in detail: In Sitapur village lives the family of Ram Khelawan Verma (70). The household consists of his wife Mithlesh Kumari (60), elder son Avneesh (36) and daughter-in-law Manisha (26), and younger son Raju (30). Ram Khelawan is a farmer, while Avneesh worked in a finance company in the city. Younger son Raju works in a private job in Mumbai. Chief representative Suresh Chandra reported, ‘For the past few days, Ram Khelawan had been quarreling with his son over not helping with farming and money matters. Ram Khelawan was upset about this. On Wednesday morning, when daughter-in-law Manisha returned home after cutting fodder from the field, she had a dispute with her mother-in-law over something. An argument started between the two.’ Father brought licensed gun from the room During the argument, Avnish and Ramkhelawan reached the spot. Avnish tried to resolve the dispute, which angered his father Ramkhelawan. After this, a fight started between father and son. Meanwhile, Ramkhelawan brought out his double barrel licensed gun from the room. Before anyone could understand anything, he opened fire. First he fired at Avnish. When daughter-in-law Manisha ran to save him, he shot her too. The bullet hit Manisha in the stomach, causing her to fall unconscious on the ground. While Avnish was shot near the shoulder. Both fell to the ground drenched in blood and became unconscious. Both were taken to the hospital by car The broad daylight firing caused panic in the village. Hearing the sound of gunshots, people from the neighborhood rushed to the spot. A large crowd of villagers gathered outside Ram Khelawan's house. The villagers picked up the blood-soaked husband and wife, put them in a car and took them to CHC Bindki. Where during treatment, doctors declared Avinash dead. While seeing Manisha's critical condition, she was referred to the district hospital. Manisha was referred to Kanpur from the district hospital. Accused father fled from the scene with a bicycle Meanwhile, after committing the crime, the accused Ram Khelawan remained present at the house for about 45 minutes. On receiving information, Bindki Kotwali police reached the spot. Seeing the police arrive, he fled on a bicycle. The police have seized the accused's gun and taken it into custody. Bindki Kotwali Inspector said - After a dispute at home, the father shot him with a licensed gun. The police have recovered and seized the licensed gun used in the incident. The accused Ram Khilawan is absconding, and police teams have been deployed for his arrest. The son's body has been sent for post-mortem.

stories.title: Akhilesh says Tinnu Yadav wrongly linked as relative:Slams Brajesh Pathak, takes dig at his emotional display
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday said that there has been massive corruption at the place of Lord Shri Ram, and CCTV footage has gone missing. He further alleged that worse things are being done now, and if a surname like ‘Yadav’ is found in a name, it is being wrongly linked as a relative. He said this is shameful. Actually, UP minister OP Rajbhar had said that Akhilesh raised the issue of alleged theft in the Ram Temple. He also claimed that the first name that came up in the theft case was Tinnu Yadav, and that Tinnu informed Akhilesh about the theft and asked him to give a statement. In a press conference in Lucknow, without naming him, Akhilesh took a dig at Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, saying people were shedding “fake tears”. He said tears appear only when cameras are on and stop when cameras are off. He added that the pain of losing a child is the greatest pain, and unless someone has experienced such a loss, they cannot understand it. Notably, the Deputy CM had become emotional while speaking to the media after the recent accident. Akhilesh said that government officials and the Chief Minister’s close aides are responsible for the incident. He alleged that officials took the Chief Minister to the accident site to protect themselves. He said the government should learn lessons from every incident and provide help to victims’ families, demanding ₹1 crore compensation for the deceased children’s families. Akhilesh Yadav also commented on the Ram Mandir donation theft case, saying that people are watching everything in Ayodhya and it is a matter of public faith. He said now no one will speak about donations because agencies like ED and CBI will be sent after them. He claimed many people are involved in the Ayodhya matter and added that even CM Yogi used to visit Ayodhya frequently, yet was not informed about the alleged irregularities. Key Points from Akhilesh's Press Conference Unable to conduct Pradhan elections, what will they conduct assembly elections first He said those who cannot even conduct village head (pradhan) elections properly cannot be expected to hold assembly elections. He alleged that farmers are not getting fertilisers like DAP and that the government is conducting surveys only to estimate its electoral prospects. He said corruption has become the government’s “religion” and hospitals are in a critical condition, comparing them to patients on ventilators. He also referred to pressure on doctors at KGMU. Will install a gold statue of Maharani Durgavati Akhilesh said that India has produced great courageous women and announced that if his party forms government, a gold statue of Maharani Durgavati will be installed at the riverfront. He added that gold will become cheaper in India and more accessible. Will give tribals rights and respect according to their population He also said that tribals will be given rights and respect according to their population through a census. He promised administrative reforms including certificates being issued at villages, CBIs probe into tribal killings, housing support, free education from KG to PG, reservation in tenders, separate commissions, hostels, and even a separate police station for tribal communities. He also promised scholarships and foreign education support for meritorious students. Administrative failure in Ram Mandir case Akhilesh further alleged that the government wants to change the Constitution and is trying to gather MPs for this purpose. He said the Ram Mandir case reflects administrative failure and commented sarcastically that “SIT means Share in Theft and damage in trust,” calling it a serious lapse and an insult to faith. He also said that the government is travelling to Bengaluru under the name of investment and claimed the government’s exit is certain. He questioned where investment and jobs are, saying elections are near so no real investment will come. Going to Bangalore under the pretext of investment, government's days are numbered On the Aaliganj incident, Akhilesh said that if the government had acted earlier, children’s lives could have been saved. He alleged selective action, saying bulldozers are used against the poor while being spared for influential people. He also claimed that rescue agencies failed to respond in time. On Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, he said “engines are colliding,” alleging internal conflicts within the BJP are being highlighted.

stories.title: DDU included in THE Rankings 1001–1500 band:Secures top 500 position in ‘Zero Hunger’ and ‘Clean Energy’ categories
stories.summary: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University (DDU) has delivered a strong performance in the Times Higher Education (THE) Sustainability Impact Rankings 2026, earning global recognition. The university has shown a significant improvement in its ranking. Last year, DDU was placed in the 1501+ band, but this year it has improved to the 1001–1500 band. In addition, under the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the university has secured a place among the world’s top 500 universities in two categories — ‘Zero Hunger’ (SDG 2) and ‘Affordable and Clean Energy’ (SDG 7). Only 5 state universities from UP got a place This year’s ranking assessed 1,603 universities worldwide, out of which 110 universities from India were included. Among Uttar Pradesh’s state universities, only five government universities made it to the list, with Gorakhpur University marking its strong presence. The ranking is based on the contribution of universities towards the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including performance in research, teaching, governance, resource conservation, and community engagement. Success achieved due to these efforts According to DDU administration, this success is the result of integrating academics, research, and administration with social responsibility. The university has been actively working in areas such as nutrition, food security, environmental protection, energy conservation, women empowerment, healthcare, rural development, and skill development. Through platforms like NSS and NCC, the university is also promoting social awareness and encouraging innovation and research-based initiatives. Result of Governor's guidance and teamwork The university has credited this achievement to the guidance of Uttar Pradesh Governor and Chancellor Anandiben Patel, stating that her vision has helped the institution become more socially and environmentally responsible. DDU will rise even higher in the future - Vice Chancellor On this achievement, Vice Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon congratulated all teachers, researchers, students, and staff members. She said the recognition reflects the hard work of the entire university community and expressed confidence that DDU will achieve even higher global rankings in the future.

stories.title: Haryanvi dancer attacked in Bulandshahr:Bike-borne men smash car windows with sticks, victim cries ‘there is a limit to shamelessness’
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancer Dimple Chaudhary was attacked in Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr. She claims that two youths hit her vehicle with a stick and broke the front windshield. She had earlier also received phone threats. The dancer says she will file a police complaint in this case. A crying video of Dimple Chaudhary has also surfaced, in which she is seen saying, “There is a limit to shamelessness. I was going to my sister’s house. They damaged my car like this.” Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Dimple said she was extremely scared after the attack and became unconscious, due to which she had to be taken to hospital. She added that she had received threats earlier as well, but police did not take action. Now, she said, police are waiting for a major incident to happen. Dimple Chaudhary also showed the broken windshield of her car in the video. Now know what Dimple Chaudhary said... Was going to sister's house Dimple Chaudhary said that on Monday she was going to her younger sister’s place. She had stopped at a CNG pump in Sikandrabad where her brother bought cold drink and chips. After that, she left again for her sister’s house in Sikandrabad. During this time, she was also talking to a friend on phone. Became unconscious after the attack, was taken to hospital Dimple said the life-threatening attack took place around 11:30 pm. The attackers targeted her Brezza car and then two bike-borne men fled from the spot. After the incident, she was extremely frightened and fainted. Her younger brother and driver, in a panic, took her to Naveen Hospital. After that, she did not go to her sister’s house and returned home. No action taken on previous complaint The dancer further said that when she had earlier received phone threats, she had gone to the police outpost and filed a complaint. She had also spoken to a police officer on call, but she was made to sit at the police station for about two hours. When the concerned person did not return, she left for home. No action was taken in that case either, and now she has faced a life-threatening attack. Police waiting for a major accident She alleged that police are waiting for a major incident to happen and her life remains under constant threat. She said she had no bodyguard at the time of attack, nor any weapon in the vehicle. The attackers could have killed her. She added that she will file a complaint today at the police station and meet the SP tomorrow. Threatened with a call on June 18 On 18 June, Dimple Chaudhary had also received a threatening phone call. She said the caller identified himself as a “don from Chambal”. The caller had said, “I will kidnap you from your home. An AK-47 will come out of your house.” She shared two audio-video clips of this call on her social media account. First Recording Caller: Madam, I saw your reel. Dancer: The whole world watches reels, that doesn't mean you should call me. Caller: I have fallen in love with you. Dancer: I will abuse you very badly. You are being disrespectful. Why do you use such words that force me to abuse or speak wrongly? Have you fallen in love in your old age? Where did you get my number from? Caller: I will get an AK-47 out of your house. Dancer: Say that again, what were you saying? Caller - If you want to record, go ahead and record, there's no problem, okay. Dancer: What do you mean, AK-47 will come out of the house. Second Recording Dancer: Why are you harassing me? Caller: I will forcibly pick you up from your home. Dancer: How can you forcibly pick me up from home like this? Caller: I am a powerful man and a dacoit of Chambal? Dancer: If you are from Chambal, then how can you forcibly pick me up? Caller: After picking you up, I'll tell you how I can pick you up. Dancer: I didn't tell you to. Nor am I recording you. iPhone doesn't even have recording. Caller: I also have an iPhone, are you thinking that only you have an iPhone. Dancer: I have never seen you, nor have I ever met you, so how did you fall in love with me? Caller: Do you want to record this and play it to the police? Let me tell you, this is the don of Chambal. Dancer: I swear on my brother, I have not done any recording?

stories.title: Late-night horror in Meerut:Girl allegedly forced into SUV; scooty riders rammed while chasing vehicle
stories.summary: In Meerut, a group of men allegedly abducted a young woman in a Scorpio SUV on Tuesday night. The incident took place near Brahmpuri Metro Station at around 11:30 pm when the accused reportedly arrived in a vehicle and forcibly dragged the woman inside. The woman began screaming for help. Hearing the commotion, some young men riding a scooter rushed towards the Scorpio. Fearing they would be caught, the accused sped away. In the process, the SUV hit the scooter before accelerating and fleeing from the spot. The youths then began chasing the vehicle. The youths claimed that while they were following the Scorpio, one of its doors remained open. The woman was allegedly screaming loudly and pleading for help. However, due to the vehicle's high speed, they could only follow it up to Rithani. The Scorpio then headed towards Partapur. The youths later informed the police about the incident. Police have started examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area. In the preliminary investigation, police have denied that it was a kidnapping. Officials said the facts of the case would become clear only after the vehicle is traced and recovered. A video showed the accused driving away with the Scorpio's door open after allegedly taking the woman away. Now understand the entire case in a sequential manner- Rohit Kapoor, a resident of Saraswati Lok and treasurer of the Transport Association, said that he was returning home from his office in Transport Nagar with his associate Ekansh Goyal on Tuesday night. A vehicle was parked near Brahmpuri Metro Station and they had just crossed it when they heard someone shouting from behind, “Look, they have taken a woman away. Catch them, catch them.” Moments later, a speeding vehicle passed by them. Rohit said he somehow managed to save his scooter and move aside. The scooter also slipped slightly. After regaining control, he noticed that the vehicle's door was open. When he chased it, he could hear cries of “Save me, save me” coming from inside. However, the vehicle kept moving farther away and he eventually had to stop. He managed to note that the registration number began with “DL” and ended with “7060”, but could not see the middle digits. CCTV footage showed the woman inside the same Scorpio, with its doors open. Chased on scooter for 3km Rohit said they followed the vehicle for nearly 3 kilometres and also recorded a video during the chase. The accused continued driving with the Scorpio's door open. Once the SUV had moved too far ahead, they informed the police. Rohit Kapoor claimed that the woman inside the vehicle was repeatedly pleading for help. Girl seen getting out of the same Scorpio in CCTV SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosale said CCTV footage had been examined and confirmed that the Scorpio had passed through the TP Nagar police station area. A woman and a child were already present inside the vehicle. When the vehicle reached Brahmpuri Metro Station and its door opened, people nearby reportedly heard arguments and sounds of a quarrel from inside the SUV. They then alerted the police. He said that taking the matter seriously, four teams from TP Nagar and Brahmpuri police stations had been formed. The SWAT team is searching for the vehicle. However, based on the CCTV footage examined so far, there is no evidence at first glance that a woman was forcibly dragged into the vehicle and taken away.

stories.title: Burqa-clad woman visits temple, says ‘Baba called me’:Joins aarti in Shahjahanpur, chants ‘Jai Shri Shyam’
stories.summary: A woman wearing a burqa entered a temple in Uttar Pradesh’s Shahjahanpur and participated in the evening aarti. She remained inside the temple for around 15 minutes and stood among other devotees with folded hands. During this time, a young man noticed her presence. The man asked her, “How did you come to the temple? How did you become a devotee of Baba?” The woman replied, “Baba called me, so I came.” He then said, “If you have come to the temple, you should also chant Baba’s slogan.” Without hesitation, the woman responded with a loud “Jai Shri Shyam”. After the aarti concluded, the woman left for her home. However, her identity has not yet been established. The incident took place at the Khatu Shyam Temple in the Kotwali area. Although it occurred on Monday, the video surfaced on Wednesday. See 3 pictures- Woman stood in temple with folded hands The Khatu Shyam Temple is located near Bareilly Mor in Shahjahanpur city, where the evening aarti is held daily between 7:30 pm and 7:45 pm. Devotees from nearby districts also visit the temple regularly. The video, which is around one minute long, shows the woman arriving at the temple during Monday evening’s aarti while wearing a burqa. At the time, devotees were standing with folded hands during the prayers. The woman also stood on a mat spread across the temple floor and joined them in prayer. She was carrying a blue basket containing prasad. During the aarti, a young man asked where she had come from. The woman said she was from Jamour village in the Kant block area.

stories.title: ‘Mummy, save me’, Bhavish screamed till his last breath:Mother hears son’s final cries on video call before Lucknow fire death
stories.summary: The last rites of 23-year-old Bhavish Sharma, who lost his life in the devastating Lucknow fire tragedy, were performed at his native village Mahipur in Sonipat on Tuesday. As soon as her son's body reached the family home, his mother Sonia broke down in tears. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Sonia recalled her final video call with Bhavish. She said her son had taken on family responsibilities at a very young age. That was why he had moved to a big city like Lucknow for a job that paid just ₹25,000 a month. Fighting back tears, she said: "Till his last moments, Bhavish kept saying to me, ‘Mummy, save me... save me...’ but I could do nothing. My son kept suffering. I ran around the house helplessly, but there was nothing I could do. How could I save him?" According to the family, Bhavish had completed a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from Supva in Rohtak last year. He was also preparing for postgraduate studies. He had always been a brilliant student and dreamed of going abroad. To support that dream, his father sold his library and bought him an iPhone and a computer. Pleaded for help, crying “Mummy, Mummy” on video call Sonia said Bhavish called her at 2:32 pm on Monday. He was screaming “Mummy, Mummy” on a video call. She could not see anything except thick smoke. "I told him, ‘Son, I can't see anything.’ He replied, ‘Mummy, there is a fire here.’ I said, ‘I can't even see your face.’ He then said, ‘Mummy, it will be difficult to survive.’ I told him, ‘Son, jump from somewhere above.’ He replied, ‘Mummy, people are starting to die here.’" Crying uncontrollably, Sonia said, "Till the very end, Bhavish kept saying, ‘Mummy, save me... save me...’ but I could do nothing." Soon after, the phone disconnected and that became their last conversation. A few hours later, her son returned home not alive, but as a body. Wanted to support his father and arrange his sister’s wedding Sonia said Bhavish had happily boarded a bus from Delhi on June 6 to join his job in Lucknow. He was the only son in the family and had one sister, Trisha. He wanted to arrange a grand wedding for her. He had accepted the job believing he could support his father and ensure his sister’s marriage was conducted well. "I never imagined that my son, who spoke about becoming our support, would never return. Had I known this, I would never have let him go so far away." People carrying Bhavish’s body for the funeral procession in Mahipur village on Tuesday. Father Narendra shares his son's dreams Joining letter came on June 5 Narendra Sharma said, "I have been working as a Hindi teacher in a private school for the past 25 years, while my wife Sonia has been doing stitching work from home for the last 15 years." He said that when Bhavish received his appointment letter on June 5, he was away in the village. Bhavish called him and said, "Papa, when are you coming home? I have good news for you." When Narendra returned home that night, Bhavish happily informed him that he had secured his first job. He also told his father that he needed a computer and an iPhone. Despite the family's financial difficulties, Narendra did not want his son's dreams to be shattered. To arrange the money, he sold his Gloria Library located on Thana Road in Kharkhoda. Using the money from the sale, he bought a computer worth ₹2.5 lakh and an iPhone for Bhavish. He had been hired as a junior artist with a monthly salary of ₹25,000. Bhavish was also learning Japanese. His dream was to go abroad and study advanced technology-related courses. Wanted to go abroad to learn advanced technology Narendra said Bhavish was learning Japanese and aspired to pursue advanced technology courses overseas. For this, he was also attending online coaching classes from abroad, spending between ₹12,000 and ₹15,000 every month. The family had already sold nearly one bigha of land to fund his education. Now only one kila and two bighas of land remain in the village. “Whenever I remember those dreams today, my eyes fill with tears. I have not just lost my son; I have lost every moment of my life.” Uncle Rajnish narrated the story of the accident Friends kept crying while hugging his belongings Bhavish's uncle Rajneesh said that Bhavish had rented a room in the Alibagh area, about 300 metres from his office. He lived there with three friends. When the family reached Lucknow to collect his belongings, his friends broke down and clung to his possessions. They had witnessed their friend's death with their own eyes. Two of Bhavish’s roommates were also trapped in the same building. One survived by jumping down from the building, while another climbed down using an electric wire that had no current flowing through it. Both suffered injuries to their hands and legs. The two friends said they kept calling out Bhavish’s name, but by then the entire building had filled with smoke. Rajneesh said there were no burn marks on Bhavish’s body. He died due to suffocation. Death occurred due to suffocation, not fire Rajneesh said the entire building had been reduced to ashes. The fire had started on the first floor, while all the youngsters were trapped on the second floor. "No one died from burns. Everyone died due to suffocation. The Yogi government and the administration provided considerable support. There was not a single burn mark on Bhavish’s body. He died because of suffocation. During his final conversation with his mother, he could see death approaching." At the time of the incident, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was in Aligarh and was scheduled to stay there overnight. However, as soon as he received news of the fire, he travelled directly from Aligarh to Aliganj in Lucknow. Seeing the scene, he became emotional. Every eye became moist when the body reached the village At around 3:20 am on Tuesday, family members left Lucknow with the body for Mahipur village. Nearly ten hours later, Bhavish’s mortal remains reached his native village. A large crowd had gathered there. As soon as Sonia saw her son's body, she broke down. His sister was inconsolable. Every villager wanted to pay their final respects. His friends, who had graduated with him from Rohtak last year, also attended the funeral. His friends said this was not merely an accident but a death caused by negligence. The family and friends demanded that those responsible for failing to maintain safety arrangements at institutions should face serious charges equivalent to culpable homicide.

stories.title: Free IAS, PCS, NEET coaching in UP:Check district-wise centres across all 75 districts; know how to apply
stories.summary: If you want to become a government officer but cannot afford expensive coaching, the ‘Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana’ could help. Applications have started in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Classes will begin between July 1 and July 15 and will continue until April 30, 2027. Under this scheme, free coaching is provided for several competitive examinations, including UPSC, PCS, NDA, NEET and JEE. Selection is done through two methods. The first is direct admission, while the second is based on merit, interview or an entrance examination. This means that if a centre has 50 seats and only 35 students apply, all applicants may get direct admission. However, if applications exceed the number of available seats, selection is made through merit, an interview or an entrance test. The decision is taken by the District Social Welfare Officer or the Chief Development Officer (CDO) of the concerned district. What is the complete application process for this scheme? Which documents are required? Here is everything you need to know. How to apply in two ways Online- Offline- These documents are required Hostel and mess facilities along with free coaching Students belonging to the SC, ST or OBC categories who wish to prepare for IAS or PCS examinations can also get hostel and mess facilities in addition to free coaching. For this, they must qualify an entrance examination. The test is conducted in all 18 divisions of the state and includes graduation-level questions. 5 major features of the scheme Free study material: Selected students receive free books, digital content and access to e-learning platforms. Guidance from officers: IAS, IPS and PCS officers posted in districts regularly conduct classes and share preparation strategies with students. Virtual and physical classes: Offline classes are conducted at divisional and district levels. Recorded lectures are also available on the Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana YouTube channel and portal. Doubt-clearing sessions: Special counselling and question-and-answer sessions are organised for students. Tablets and smartphones: Several meritorious students who study regularly under the scheme are provided tablets or smartphones by the government. The scheme was started in 2021 The Uttar Pradesh Government launched the Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana on February 16, 2021. The scheme is currently operational in all 75 districts of the state. There are also plans to expand it to the tehsil and block levels in the future, and the government is continuously working towards that goal. See the list of main centers in major cities below-

stories.title: SIT names 17 in Ram Mandir donation theft case:Champat Rai under scanner, FIR may follow; trust overhaul recommended
stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Temple donation theft case, the Special Investigation Team (SIT), in its probe report, has reportedly named 17 people as accused, including temple trust General Secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr Anil Mishra and construction in-charge Gopal Rao. Sources said an FIR against them is considered almost certain. The SIT is also expected to reach Ayodhya again today for further investigation. Meanwhile, on Tuesday evening, a ceremonial flag-hoisting was held atop the Sheshavatar Temple spire within the Ram Temple complex. Eleven saints conducted the flag worship amid Vedic chants. Dr Anil Mishra and construction in-charge Gopal Rao welcomed the saints. The event was coordinated by Champat Rai. Around 4,000 people attended. Both Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya were expected to participate, but they cancelled their visit following the deaths of 15 children in the Lucknow fire tragedy. SIT investigation report sent to PMO The SIT submitted its investigation report to the state government on Tuesday. According to sources, it recommends registering an FIR and reconstituting the temple trust. It has also suggested appointing a senior bureaucrat as the temple’s CEO. The team said the initial report runs to 20 pages and includes details of questioning around 150 people. Sources added that the SIT has recommended an audit of donations received over the last five years and proposed measures to prevent irregularities in donation handling. Questions have also been raised over the role of trust office-bearers. According to sources, the report has been forwarded by the state government to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The PMO will decide which trust members should be retained or removed. Donation box keys allegedly found with Ramshankar alias Tinnu Sources said the SIT found the keys to the donation boxes in the possession of Ramshankar alias Tinnu during the investigation. The SIT has identified around 150 sevadars and employees linked to the matter. It is alleged that since the consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla on 22 January 2024, the financial status of several of them has changed rapidly, with some reportedly becoming millionaires. According to sources, the assets of Phoolkant Mishra, considered close to Champat Rai, have also increased significantly. He reportedly owns three luxury cars worth around ₹25 lakh and has seen a noticeable change in lifestyle, placing him under the SIT’s scanner. How the Ram Temple theft was exposed According to sources, embezzlement had allegedly been taking place in the temple for years. Sevadars were aware of the alleged misappropriation but remained silent because influential individuals were allegedly involved. Over the past two years, as Tinnu’s influence within the temple grew, a section of temple workers reportedly became unhappy. This group allegedly developed close ties with him, gathered information and eventually passed details to the media. It was after this that the alleged donation theft came to light. Recovery of 2 crores so far, estimated theft of 200 crores In the Ram Temple theft case, around ₹2 crore has reportedly been recovered based on information provided by five accused — Lavkush, Avneesh, Anukalp, Karune and Ramshankar alias Tinnu. Gold was also allegedly recovered from Tinnu’s house, who is said to be close to Champat Rai. Preliminary estimates suggest the theft could exceed ₹200 crore. SP chief and former minister had raised the issue of theft

stories.title: Demolition order was issued against Lucknow building but later revoked:Culpable homicide case against owner, action against 18 officials
stories.summary: At least 15 people have died in the fire that broke out in a two-storey building in Lucknow. The investigation has revealed that the building where the blaze occurred was allegedly illegal. Authorities said a demolition order had been issued against the structure in 2016, but the order was later revoked. On Wednesday, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) pasted a notice on the building. LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the owner has been asked to respond within 15 days. He added that the building will be demolished. The property belongs to Virendra Shukla, owner of Rameshwaram Institute of Technology and Management. Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and arrested four accused, including Virendra Shukla. Six LDA officials have been suspended, while notices have been sent to the state government against 18 officials. Earlier on Tuesday morning, an SIT and a forensic team reached the site to investigate the tragedy. The SIT, comprising IAS officer Amrit Abhijat and IPS officer Praveen Kumar, inspected the building and collected evidence in bags from the spot. Following the incident, police and administrative authorities have launched statewide inspections of coaching centres and hotels. So far, 48 coaching institutes and three hotels have been sealed for failing to meet fire safety requirements. What was operating inside the building? The building is located in Lucknow’s Aliganj area. The basement, ground floor and first floor housed a pet shop and clinic. The second floor contained a facility called “Learning Space”, used as a library and coaching centre, along with Head Hopper Studio, which works in 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. stories.title: Bhaskar reporter visits Lucknow fire site:Two-storey building had no windows or exhausts, door was double-locked
stories.summary: Fifteen people died of suffocation in the fire that broke out in a Lucknow building. All of them desperately tried to escape, but could not get out due to thick smoke and the locked gate. Bhaskar reporters entered the Head Hopper Studio, from where 15 bodies were recovered, to investigate the scene. The conditions inside were found to be horrific. The two-storey building, constructed on just 185 square metres of land, had neither windows nor exhaust systems. As a result, when the fire broke out, smoke filled the entire structure. The biometric double-lock gate of the coaching centre on the second floor got jammed. People trapped inside rushed into the washrooms in an attempt to save themselves. However, the washrooms too filled with smoke. After some time, as the wooden structures inside the studio caught fire, glass panels shattered and fell. Despite this, the smoke could not escape from the building. Fire brigade officials and personnel entered by breaking through the rear wall of the building and found bodies lying on top of one another. The team recovered all 15 bodies one by one. See 3 pictures... Spark originated from short circuit in basement AC The investigation has revealed that the fire originated in the basement of the building. A short circuit in the outdoor unit of an air-conditioner triggered the blaze. Within moments, the entire building was engulfed in smoke and flames. The basement was being used as a warehouse for a pet shop and contained a large quantity of goods. Several pets were also present there. Three motorcycles were parked next to the AC outdoor unit. All these factors contributed to the rapid spread of the fire. Smoke filled all floors due to lack of ventilation Investigators found that 23 people were inside the building at the time of the incident. Amid the smoke and fire, seven people managed to escape using wires as support. One young man jumped from the upper floor and is currently undergoing treatment. The remaining 15 people were trapped inside and died. According to investigating officials, the absence of ventilation caused smoke to accumulate across all floors. Those trapped inside could not find a way out. Most of the deaths were caused not by burns but by suffocation due to toxic smoke. Forensic experts and local police officers also visited the studio and collected evidence. People trapped on the second floor kept struggling to get out Investigators found that different activities were being conducted on different floors of the building. The basement, ground floor and first floor housed a pet shop and clinic. The second floor had a library called Learning Space and Head Hopper Studio. The studio was engaged in 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. The floor also contained a kitchen, cabins, washrooms and a large number of computers. After the fire spread, people on this floor were the ones who struggled the most to get out. The fire reportedly intensified due to materials stored in the pet shop warehouse in the basement. Biometric gate locked, stairs to the roof were padlocked One of the most serious findings in the investigation is that a metal channel gate had been installed on the staircase leading to the roof. However, it was locked. As a result, smoke could not escape upwards. In addition, the studio’s main entrance operated through a biometric system and became locked during the incident. Investigators believe that if access to the roof had been open, several people might have been able to save themselves. The bodies were recovered after rescuers broke through the rear wall of the building. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also visited the site late on the night of 22 June (Monday). 20 Fire Brigade Vehicles Conducted 8-Hour Rescue Operation The building’s single access route and lack of ventilation created significant challenges for rescue teams. More than 20 fire brigade vehicles remained engaged in the operation for nearly eight hours. During firefighting efforts, water accumulated throughout the building, affecting rescue operations. Teams eventually broke through the rear wall to gain entry and then recovered the bodies from inside. SIT and Forensic Team Arrived for Investigation A two-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to probe the incident. Principal Secretary (Housing and Urban Planning) Amrit Abhijat and ADG Lucknow Zone Praveen Kumar, both members of the SIT, visited the site on 23 June (Tuesday). ADG Praveen Kumar said that evidence has been gathered and statements will be recorded from eyewitnesses, building operators and victims’ families. Once the investigation is complete, details regarding the causes of the incident and those responsible will be made public. A separate inquiry committee formed by the Lucknow Development Authority is also examining the building’s construction, map approval, fire safety compliance and exit arrangements. Preliminary findings suggest serious lapses in adherence to safety norms.

stories.title: Triple murder accused listened to 'Dhurandhar' song after killings:Niece says he killed her parents and little brother with a cleaver
stories.summary: “Daddy, Mummy and Babu were sleeping together at night. Suddenly, I heard a loud thud in the room. I woke up immediately. I saw Daddy had fallen on me. Uncle was attacking his neck with a cleaver. I got frightened and moved aside. Then Uncle struck Mummy on the head with an iron rod and later slit her throat with the cleaver. After that, Uncle picked up my little brother Reyansh. I begged him, ‘Please leave Babu.’ But he cut Babu’s throat as well. Blood was everywhere. I started crying in fear. Then Uncle warned me that if I told anyone, he would do the same to me. After that, he took a bath and listened to a song from the film Dhurandhar on his phone." These chilling details were narrated by a nine-year-old girl who witnessed the murder of her parents and younger brother. The triple murder took place in Bansgaon, Gorakhpur, at around 3 am on 22 June. A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his elder brother Amit Gupta (35), sister-in-law Ranjana (32), and three-year-old nephew Reyansh while they slept. Eyewitness daughter recounts the horror The couple’s nine-year-old daughter, Jyoti, told police that after killing her parents and brother, her uncle approached her. “His entire body was covered in blood. He came towards me and tied a cloth over my mouth. He warned me not to tell anyone, otherwise he would kill me too,” she said. According to Jyoti, her uncle then went into the courtyard, bathed, changed his clothes and climbed onto the roof. “There he sat listening to the song ‘Gehra Hua.’ from the film Dhurandhar on his mobile phone,' she said. Grandmother fainted after seeing the bodies Terrified, Jyoti ran to her grandparents and informed them about the murders. “I was trembling with fear. I told Grandma Anita Devi that Uncle had killed Mummy, Daddy and Babu,” she said. Anita Devi immediately rushed to the room with her granddaughter. Seeing the bodies lying on the bed, she screamed and then fainted. Grandfather Harilal Gupta arrived moments later and raised the alarm before informing the police. Police found the accused on the roof A police team reached the house within about 20 minutes of receiving the information. While officers began searching for the accused, Jyoti informed them that her uncle was sitting on the roof using his mobile phone. When police attempted to access the roof through the staircase, they found the door locked from inside. Officers then climbed onto the roof through a neighbouring house. According to police, the accused began crying when he saw officers approaching him. Jyoti said she has been unable to sleep since the murders. “On Monday night, I could not sleep without my mother, father and brother. My uncle’s face kept appearing in my dreams,” she said. She recalled that her parents wanted her to become a doctor. “Mummy and Daddy always said I should become a doctor and make the family proud. Who will say those things to me now?” she asked. Child’s statement recorded on video Bansgaon police have recorded Jyoti’s statement on video. Preparations are now underway to record her statement before a court as well. According to police officials, a charge sheet is expected to be filed within the next three to four days so that the trial process can proceed swiftly. Accused asked for food after reaching juvenile home On 22 June, police produced the 16-year-old accused before a court, which subsequently sent him to a juvenile correctional facility. Police escorted him to the juvenile home in Shahpur. Officials said the teenager repeatedly stated that he felt no remorse over the killings and remarked that he would at least receive regular meals in custody. He was admitted to the facility at around 5.30 pm and immediately asked for food. Authorities have placed him under special surveillance and housed him separately from other inmates. Family performs last rites amid grief The last rites of Amit Gupta and Ranjana were performed on Monday at Dhobia Ghat. Their father, Harilal Gupta, lit the funeral pyres of his son and daughter-in-law. The body of three-year-old Reyansh was immersed in water according to religious customs. A large number of relatives, villagers and local residents attended the funeral. The sight of three coffins being carried together cast a pall of grief over the entire area. Police personnel were deployed at the cremation ground, while family members struggled to cope with their loss. South Gorakhpur SP Dinesh Puri said the murder weapons, including the cleaver and iron rod allegedly used in the attack, have been recovered. He said, ‘A charge sheet in the case will be filed very soon’ Accused teenager’s confession According to police, the accused claimed he had once been a bright student. ‘I was very good at studies. Until Class 5, I always stood first in my class in a CBSE school. I wanted to become an officer through the UPSC examination,’ he reportedly said. The teenager alleged that his father later made him leave school. 'I somehow continued studying while working as a labourer. I never got enough time to study and failed Class 10 again,' he said. He further claimed that family members constantly taunted and humiliated him. ‘For many days I was not even given food. I had to look for a place to sleep in my own house. That is why I decided to finish everyone. I had planned to torture and kill my father as well,’ he allegedly told investigators. Father demands death penalty Harilal Gupta, who lost his son, daughter-in-law and grandson in the attack, has demanded the strictest possible punishment for the accused. Weeping inconsolably, he appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure that his younger son receives the death penalty. “My younger son kept demanding money from me. We often argued over it. If he wanted to kill someone, he should have killed me. What wrong had my elder son done to him?” Harilal said. He added that he is undergoing treatment for cancer, while his wife is receiving treatment for a heart condition. “In such circumstances, I could not always give him money. He never understood that. He only thought about himself and had no concern for the family,” he said. No one should have such a child Anita Devi repeatedly lost consciousness while recalling the incident. Overcome with grief, she said, “God should never give anyone a child like this. He has destroyed the entire family.” As the investigation continues, police are preparing to file the charge sheet, while a traumatised nine-year-old girl remains the sole eyewitness to one of the most shocking family murders the region has witnessed in recent years.

stories.title: Cricketer Akash Deep's marriage in Varanasi:Mandap decorated in Shiva Temple theme; Dhirendra Shastri connects via video call
stories.summary: Indian fast bowler Akash Deep is set to get married today in Varanasi (Kashi). The wedding ceremony is being held at Taj Ganges Hotel. Both Akash Deep and his fiancée Akshita Raj are originally from Sasaram (Rohtas) in Bihar. Just four days ago, the Bihar government appointed Akash Deep as DSP. The wedding mandap has been decorated with a Shiva temple theme. Early on Wednesday, Akash Deep and his fiancée arrived in Varanasi with their families. Around 350 guests are expected to attend the ceremony. All guests have been sent QR codes for entry, which must be scanned at the hotel gate. A specially curated wedding meal, priced at around ₹4,500 per plate, will be served, featuring a mix of Banarasi and international cuisines. Makeup artists from Delhi have been brought in to prepare the bride and groom. Earlier, pre-wedding rituals were performed at home in the presence of close family members and relatives, with traditional music, drums and celebrations. The ceremony has been kept largely private, with media access restricted, although several personalities from the cricket world may attend. Akash Deep also spoke to spiritual leader Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri via video call ahead of the wedding, who wished him a happy married life. He had earlier also interacted with Jagadguru Rambhadracharya for blessings. Some photos from the wedding celebrations show traditional rituals being performed, including the Kuwarth ceremony conducted by his aunt, as well as festive preparations with band and music outside his residence. See some pictures related to the Mehendi function- Tilak ceremony held on 22 June A Tilak ceremony was organised at Akash Deep's residence on the night of 22 June. The event was attended by Bhojpuri singer Gunjan Singh and actress Kajal Raghwani. Akash Deep was also seen dancing with family members and guests during the celebrations. Several prominent personalities attended the function, including Rohtas MP Manoj Kumar and MLA Murari Prasad Gautam. See some pictures from the Tilak ceremony- Bollywood-themed decorations at the cricketer's home Akash Deep's residence has been decorated with a Bollywood-inspired theme for the wedding celebrations. Pandals worth approximately ₹10 lakh have been constructed for the various functions. According to organisers, preparations for each ceremony take around two to three hours. A separate VIP enclosure has been created for distinguished guests attending the celebrations. See pictures of preparations at the hotel- Royal arrangements for guests at Hotel Taj in Kashi Special arrangements for guests and villagers Separate arrangements have also been made for local residents and villagers attending the festivities. Coolers, sofas, tables and chairs have been installed in all the pandals to ensure guests remain comfortable during the summer heat. In addition, professional makeup artists from Delhi have been brought in to prepare the groom for the wedding ceremonies. Check out some pictures of Akash Deep's house- Who is Akash Deep’s bride-to-be? Akshita Raj, who is set to marry Akash Deep, is a resident of Manikpur. She is the daughter of Amit Kumar Singh, popularly known as Bablu Ji, and Renu Singh, who live in Manikpur under the Indrapuri police station area. Akshita completed her Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA) and Master of Computer Applications (MCA) from the Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra. Owing to her strong academic record, she also received a job offer from the institute. However, as marriage discussions progressed during that period, she chose not to take up the position. Marriage finalised with families’ consent According to family sources, the alliance was finalised with the consent of both families. The marriage of Akash Deep and Akshita Raj has been arranged in accordance with traditional customs and rituals, under the guidance and blessings of elders from both families. With the Haldi, Mehendi and Tilak ceremonies completed, all eyes are now on the wedding ceremony in Varanasi, where the Indian fast bowler will begin a new chapter of his life alongside Akshita Raj. stories.title: Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi receives ₹1 crore offering every month:One donation box opens every day; Dimple Yadav demands Ayodhya like probe
stories.summary: The Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura receives offerings worth nearly ₹1 crore every month. The temple trust claims that every donation made by devotees is fully secure and monitored through a transparent system, from the moment it is counted until it is deposited in the bank. The trust's clarification comes amid controversy surrounding the alleged theft of offerings worth crores of rupees from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) submitted its report on the matter to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on 23 June 2026. The issue has also entered the political arena. Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav recently questioned whether similar irregularities could be occurring at other temple projects, including the proposed Mathura-Vrindavan corridors. She alleged that the Ayodhya theft had been concealed by the government. At the same time, allegations regarding the handling of donations at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi have surfaced. Dinesh Sharma, popularly known as Falahari Baba and president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, accused the temple administration of financial irregularities. Within 24 hours of his allegations, the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan lodged an FIR against him. To understand how the temple manages and safeguards devotees' offerings, officials of the Seva Sansthan explained the entire process. Temple receives around ₹1 crore in donations every month According to Vijay Bahadur Singh, Public Relations Officer of the institution, the temple receives an average of ₹1 crore in donations each month. The funds are used for temple maintenance, decoration, staff salaries and other operational expenses. Donations are received through three channels- Pocketless uniforms and seven CCTV cameras monitor the counting process Temple officials say strict procedures are followed to ensure accountability for every rupee donated. Donation boxes opened daily The keys to all donation boxes are kept in the temple office. Every day, one donation box is opened by the counting in-charge, volunteers and security personnel. The entire process is recorded on CCTV cameras. Cash transported in sacks Money collected from the donation boxes is placed in sacks and taken to a dedicated counting room measuring approximately 15 by 15 feet. Senior officials remain present throughout the counting process. Bundles of currency notes are prepared, placed inside boxes and sealed. These sealed boxes are then moved to a treasury located within the temple premises. The treasury is monitored by seven CCTV cameras. Bank officials count and deposit the funds The following day, employees from the main branch of the State Bank visit the temple. In the presence of temple officials, the sealed boxes are opened and the cash is counted using machines. After the amount is entered into official registers, bank employees transport the funds and deposit them into the institution's account. Temple authorities maintain that the entire process is fully transparent. Employees wear special clothing Staff involved in counting donations are required to wear specially designed pocketless shirts and shorts provided by the institution. Officials say the measure prevents anyone from concealing money. Any employee who leaves the counting area during the process is thoroughly checked before re-entering. Gold and Silver audited four times a year The temple administration prepares detailed statements after separating notes and coins. Three copies of every statement are produced and maintained for record-keeping purposes. To ensure transparency, the institution conducts audits four times a year, once every three months. Valuation of precious metals Gold, silver and other precious metals received as donations are entered into a separate register and securely sealed. Once a year, experts are called in to assess the purity and market value of these items. Two organisations manage Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi 1. Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust This trust is the legal owner of the entire 13.37-acre Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi site. Approximately 2.5 acres are occupied by the Shahi Eidgah Mosque, while the remaining land remains under temple control. The trust was established on 21 February 1951 by industrialist Seth Jugal Kishore Birla. Its primary objective was to construct a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmasthan and preserve the entire site. A legal dispute regarding approximately 10.9 acres of land between the trust and the Eidgah is currently pending in court. 2. Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan This organisation oversees the temple's day-to-day administration, maintenance and operations. It was established by the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust to ensure the smooth functioning of the temple complex. The organisation was originally registered on 1 May 1958 under the name "Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sangh". In 1977, it was renamed "Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan". Its president is Mahant Nritya Gopal Das, secretary Kapil Sharma, and senior member Gopeshwar Nath Chaturvedi. The governing body also includes Joint Managing Trustee Anurag Dalmia and 15 other members. What allegations did Falahari Baba make? Dinesh Sharma, also known as Falahari Baba, who heads the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, has levelled serious allegations regarding the handling of temple donations. In a letter dated 19 June, he alleged that CCTV cameras are deliberately switched off whenever donation boxes are opened. He further claimed that cash, gold, silver and jewellery received as offerings are divided among members of the management. Demand for a CBI investigation Falahari Baba wrote a letter in his own blood demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the matter. He alleged that members of the temple management committee once travelled on scooters but now own luxury bungalows and cars worth crores of rupees. Temple administration rejects allegations The Shri Krishna Janmasthan Seva Sansthan has categorically denied all allegations, describing them as baseless and misleading. Meanwhile, the institution's Deputy Manager, Anurag Pathak, has filed a police complaint against Falahari Baba, accusing him of demanding ₹20 lakh in extortion money. The dispute has now escalated into a legal battle, even as the temple administration continues to insist that its donation management system is transparent, audited and secure.

stories.title: Couple to be wed soon die in Lucknow fire:Another girl had started a new job to support family; heartbreaking stories of victims
stories.summary: Fifteen people died of suffocation in the fire that broke out in a building in Lucknow. All of them desperately tried to escape, but could not get out because of the dense smoke and the locked exit. Bhaskar reporters entered the Head Hopper Studio, from where 15 bodies were recovered, to investigate the scene. The conditions inside appeared horrific. The two-storey building, constructed on 185 square metres of land, did not have windows or even exhaust vents. As a result, when the fire broke out, smoke quickly filled the entire building. The coaching centre on the second floor had a biometric double-lock gate, which became jammed. People trapped inside rushed into washrooms in an attempt to save themselves. However, the washrooms also filled with smoke. After some time, the wooden structures inside the studio caught fire, causing glass panels to shatter and fall. Despite this, the smoke could not escape from the building. Fire brigade officials and personnel eventually broke through the rear wall of the building to enter. Inside, the bodies were found lying on top of one another. Rescue teams recovered all 15 bodies one by one. Anamika’s father breaks down On Tuesday, Anamika’s father, Vishwanath Samanta, arrived at the post-mortem house of King George’s Medical University (KGMU). Overwhelmed with grief, he broke down repeatedly while looking at his daughter’s body. “I have lost everything. I was preparing for my daughter’s wedding, and today our family has been devastated,” he said through tears. Anamika’s mother repeatedly fainted from shock, while Vishwanath tried to comfort her despite struggling to contain his own grief. Her brother, Akash, said he had spoken to Anamika shortly before the tragedy. First, see 3 pictures- Wedding discussions were underway Vishwanath Samanta said both families had been discussing marriage. “We had visited Nilesh’s home two or three times. We met his parents and discussed the marriage. We do not know whether they were in a relationship, but they worked together in the same office. It was our wish that they get married,” he said. Akash recalled that their parents had visited Anamika in Lucknow just a week earlier. “I spoke to her on the phone in the morning. She said she was leaving for work. A few hours later, she was gone,” he said. Anamika worked as an animation artist and had been employed in Lucknow for the past three years. Before moving there, she had worked in Chandigarh. She had seven years of professional experience in the field. Silence outside Nilesh’s home A sombre silence hung over Nilesh’s house in Martinpurwa, Hazratganj. After the post-mortem examination, his body was brought home late at night and placed on a slab of ice. By morning, family members and relatives had taken him for his final rites. No family member remained at the house as neighbours mourned the young man whose wedding was expected to take place soon. Saumalya was preparing for his December wedding Another victim, Saumalya, had been planning his wedding, scheduled for December. His cousin, Shubham, travelled from West Bengal to collect the body. “We received a call from the police around 1 am informing us that Saumalya had died,” he said before breaking down in tears. Saumalya had previously worked in Ahmedabad and had moved to Lucknow two to three years ago. According to his family, he had been busy making preparations for his wedding. Anuchha observed a Monday fast before leaving for work Anuchha Rai, a resident of Dhodhankheda in Mohanlalganj, was also among those who died. Her younger sister, Isha Rai, said Monday morning was the last time they spoke. “Anuchha used to observe a fast every Monday. She would wake up early, pray and then leave for work,” Isha said. Family members had asked her to carry fruits and sabudana dishes for the fast, but she did not mention wanting to eat anything that day. Friend called to say the office was on fire Isha said her sister usually left home early and returned late, so they often spoke only in the morning or evening. At around 6 pm on Monday, Anuchha’s friend Varsha called and asked where she was. Isha replied that Anuchha was probably still at work, as her shift often continued until 7 or 7.30 pm. A short while later, Varsha called again and informed her that the office building had caught fire. “I immediately tried calling my sister’s phone. The second time, someone answered and identified himself as a police officer. He told me Anuchha’s phone was with him and asked us to come to the trauma centre immediately because the fire was very severe,” Isha said. Jyoti had started working to support her family Jyoti, a resident of Chinhat, was cremated at Baikunth Dham. Her family was inconsolable. She is survived by her parents, Hari Charan Kashyap and Kusum Kashyap, along with her four brothers. Her father runs a sweet shop in Kamta. Jyoti had joined the animation company earlier this year as a junior character artist. Family members said she had begun earning to help support the household. Eyewitness accounts of the tragedy 'People were breaking the glass with bricks' Eyewitness Kamini said panic spread rapidly after the fire broke out. “When I heard screams and came outside, there was complete chaos. People were throwing bricks at the building to break the glass and let the smoke escape. Once the glass shattered, some people tried hanging from the building and jumping down. We wanted to help but could do very little. The fire engines also arrived late, which made the situation worse,” she said. More than 50 birds and cats were inside Resident Vishal Singh Rajput said he had recently visited the pet shop operating on the ground floor. “There were more than 50 birds there, along with several cats. It was a popular pet shop and people travelled from far away to visit it,” he said. ‘The entire building was engulfed in flames’ Another eyewitness, Rahul Singh, said the fire had spread through the entire structure by the time he reached the spot. “My house is behind the building. We received information immediately. Many young people trapped inside were screaming for help,” he said. He added that the building had only one entry and exit point. ‘Both side walls were around nine inches thick, making it difficult for firefighters to break through them. The rescue operation was delayed because of this,’ he said. ‘Perhaps more lives could have been saved’ Eyewitness Abhay Maheshwari said people trapped inside desperately called for help. “The fire brigade arrived a little late. Perhaps some lives could have been saved had help reached earlier,” he said. He claimed the building had a single combined entry and exit gate, which quickly became inaccessible. “There was a pet store on the ground floor and an animation training centre above it. Many dogs and cats were also inside the shop. It is an extremely tragic incident,” he added. Three reasons the fire spread so rapidly 1. Flammable materials intensified the blaze Large quantities of pet food, plastic packaging, cardboard and other combustible materials were stored inside the pet shop. Aluminium sheets and plastic-based structures were also used in parts of the building. As a result, the fire spread rapidly and dense smoke engulfed the premises within minutes. 2. A single exit became a death trap Residents said there was only one main route for entering and exiting the building. Once smoke and flames blocked that passage, those trapped on the upper floor had virtually no means of escape. 3. No emergency exit in a multi-storey building The building lacked any alternative emergency exit. A pet shop and veterinary clinic operated on the ground floor, while a library, office and animation classes functioned upstairs. Despite accommodating large numbers of people, the building appeared to have inadequate safety arrangements. The fire broke out in Lucknow’s Aliganj area at around 2.30 pm on Monday. Fifteen people died, most of them due to suffocation caused by dense smoke. Post-mortem examinations continued for nearly seven hours, after which all bodies were handed over to their families. The investigation has revealed that the building was allegedly illegal. A demolition order had reportedly been issued against it in 2016 but was later withdrawn. Prathamesh Kumar, Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), said a notice had been served on the building owner seeking a response within 15 days. He further added after that, the building will be demolished.
