stories.title: Mahakumbh-style management at Kashi Vishwanath Dham during 'Sawan':No VIP Darshan allowed, devotees to enter through five routes
stories.summary: Preparations for Sawan (Shravan) have begun at Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi, with the temple administration making extensive arrangements in anticipation of millions of devotees during the holy month, which will be observed from 30 July to 28 August. This year, crowd management measures modelled on the Mahakumbh will be implemented to ensure the safety and convenience of pilgrims. Every Monday during Sawan, devotees will follow a five-route entry system, no-vehicle zones will be enforced, and mobile phone restrictions will remain in place. The temple administration has also announced that there will be no VIP darshan on any Monday during Sawan. To assist elderly and specially-abled devotees, e-rickshaw services will be provided, while the entire temple complex will be monitored through CCTV surveillance, additional security personnel and newly introduced Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Auspicious yogas on the first monday of Sawan The first Monday of Sawan in 2026 falls on 3 August, a day regarded as highly significant in the Hindu calendar. It coincides with Panchami Tithi of Shravan Krishna Paksha. According to astrological calculations, the day will also witness the influence of Uttarabhadrapada and Revati Nakshatra. In addition, Sukarma Yoga and Dhriti Yoga will be in effect, making the occasion especially auspicious. Throughout Sawan, Baba Vishwanath will be adorned in different forms every Monday. This year's decorations will include- E-Rickshaws for elderly and specially-abled Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Shambhu Sharan said mobile phones will be completely prohibited inside the Kashi Vishwanath Dham complex during Sawan. No devotee will be permitted to enter the temple carrying a mobile phone. Officials said the measure will strengthen security, improve crowd management and help devotees remain focused on worship. Every Monday during Sawan, the stretch between Maidagin and Godaulia will be declared a no-vehicle zone. The temple administration will operate e-rickshaw services for elderly, disabled and infirm devotees from Godaulia to Gate No. 4 and Maidagin to Gate No. 4. No VIP darshan on Sawan Mondays Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal said comprehensive security and crowd management plans are being finalised in view of the expected arrival of lakhs of devotees throughout Sawan. He said the objective is to ensure devotees receive darshan smoothly and within a shorter waiting time while avoiding long queues. Authorities are working on all aspects of entry and exit arrangements, barricading and crowd control. Existing CCTV cameras have been reviewed, and additional cameras will be installed wherever required. Deployment points for the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), paramilitary forces and the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) are also being identified. The Police Commissioner reiterated that no VIP protocol will be applicable on any Monday during Sawan. stories.title: Storms and rain in 20 UP cities, alert in 75:Lightning strike kills 7; monsoon set to arrive within 24 hours
stories.summary: The weather system responsible for the onset of the southwest monsoon has become active over Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in 20 cities across the state on Tuesday morning. Rainfall was recorded in Kanpur Nagar, Ayodhya, Gorakhpur, Bareilly, Deoria, Sitapur, Bahraich, Pilibhit, Gonda, Raebareli, Lalitpur, Chitrakoot, Farrukhabad, Jaunpur, Kanpur Dehat, Unnao, Rampur and Moradabad. Heavy rain causes waterlogging, strong winds uproot trees Heavy rainfall in Deoria and Jaunpur led to waterlogging in agricultural fields. In Gorakhpur, strong winds uprooted trees, which fell onto roads. Raebareli witnessed thunderstorms, rain and lightning. Cloudy skies prevailed across the rest of the state, bringing significant relief from the heat, with brief spells of sunshine in between. Thunderstorm and heavy rain alert issued for all 75 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rainfall alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. Heavy rainfall is likely in 38 districts, while lightning is also expected at isolated places. According to the IMD, the impact of the ongoing heatwave is expected to end from Tuesday, and the southwest monsoon could enter Uttar Pradesh at any time within the next 24 hours. Agra hottest in the state during the past 24 hours Over the past 24 hours, Agra recorded the highest temperature in the state at 42.9°C. Rainfall was reported in 15 cities, including Lucknow. In Firozabad, strong winds caused a tree to fall onto an e-rickshaw, killing five people and injuring three others. Meanwhile, lightning strikes claimed the lives of a woman in Basti and a nine-year-old child in Maharajganj. Monsoon expected to arrive around 10 days late According to the IMD, the southwest monsoon has remained stalled along the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar border for the past 19 days, but is expected to advance further on Tuesday. Once it enters the state, the first spell of heavy rainfall is likely to affect the Terai region, including Kushinagar, Maharajganj and Siddharthnagar. The monsoon typically reaches Uttar Pradesh by 20 June, but this year it is advancing around 10 days behind schedule. Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said- The monsoon is currently advancing via Motihari in Bihar. Pre-monsoon activity and light rainfall have already begun in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Terai region. From tomorrow, or between 1 and 5 July, both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh are likely to witness widespread heavy rainfall. Temperatures are expected to drop by as much as 10°C.

stories.title: Gorakhpur to get eastern UP's first NCC Training Academy:₹47.88 crore project to be completed in three months
stories.summary: The construction of Eastern Uttar Pradesh’s first state-of-the-art National Cadet Corps (NCC) Training Academy is expected to be completed within the next three months, by September 2026. The academy is being developed over a 10-acre site at Tal Kandla in Gorakhpur. A major initiative of the Yogi government, the academy is set to become a landmark institution for NCC training in the region. The project is being built at a cost of Rs 47.88 crore. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath laid the foundation stone for the academy at Tal Kandla, Gorakhpur, on 9 March 2024. Construction began in June 2024 and is scheduled for completion by September 2026. The project is being executed by Construction and Design Services, Jal Nigam, Unit-42, Gorakhpur, at a total cost of Rs 47.88 crore. According to Vivek Gupta, Project Manager of the executing agency, more than 75 per cent of the construction work has been completed. The structural work on both the administrative building and hostels has been finished, while interior finishing work is currently in progress. Facilities at the NCC training academy The academy will feature a comprehensive range of modern training and residential facilities, including- In addition, infrastructure worth Rs 7.17 crore will be developed, including the construction of a boundary wall, sentry posts on all sides, guard rooms and high-mast floodlights. Eleven districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh to benefit The NCC Group Gorakhpur, which operates under the motto "Unity and Discipline", oversees NCC activities across 11 districts of Eastern Uttar Pradesh- To train cadets from affiliated universities, schools and colleges, the group organises an average of 25 to 30 Combined Annual Training Camps (CATCs), Army Camps, Inter-Group Competitions, Republic Day Parade training programmes, and a range of social service activities every year. Notably, the National Cadet Corps (NCC) is the world's largest uniformed youth organisation, dedicated to instilling the values of unity, discipline and national service among young people.

stories.title: Man stabs friend to death in Varanasi:Dispute over dancing at wedding turns fatal; crowd beats accused
stories.summary: A young man was fatally stabbed by his own friend during a dispute while dancing to a DJ at a wedding ceremony in Varanasi on Monday night. The seriously injured victim was first taken to Jakhini Government Hospital, where he received first aid before being referred to the BHU Trauma Centre because of the severity of his injuries. The incident sparked tension in the village. Angry villagers assaulted the accused after the attack, while women and other residents later protested against the police when officers returned to the village. A heavy police presence has since been deployed in the area. The incident took place under the Mirzamurad police station limits. Argument during DJ dance turns violent According to police, a wedding ceremony was being held at the home of Ramesh Gaud, a resident of Lalpur (Ledui) village. After the groom's procession arrived, a DJ performance was underway at the Janwasa (guest accommodation for the groom's party) in Khagrampur. During the celebrations, 24-year-old Rohit Rajbhar and Anshu Vishwakarma, both residents of the village, were dancing when an argument broke out between them. The dispute quickly escalated. Police said Anshu allegedly pulled out a knife he was carrying and stabbed Rohit in the chest. Villagers catch and beat the accused Rohit collapsed to the ground, bleeding heavily, triggering panic at the wedding venue. Villagers and wedding guests present at the scene caught Anshu Vishwakarma as he attempted to flee and assaulted him before police arrived. After receiving information about the incident, officers from Mirzamurad Police Station reached the spot, rescued the accused from the crowd and took him into custody. Meanwhile, Rohit was taken to Jakhini Government Hospital by ambulance. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the BHU Trauma Centre, where he later succumbed to his injuries. Heavy police deployment after village protest The stabbing created a tense atmosphere in the village. When police returned to the village later, angry women and other residents staged a protest and forced the police team to leave the area. In view of the tension, the administration has deployed additional police personnel in the village. Police said the investigation is underway and security arrangements have been strengthened to maintain law and order.

stories.title: Police escort UP Congress chief for Ram Mandir ‘darshan’ post-house-arrest:Officers grill 'chanda chor' accused inside jail
stories.summary: The political controversy surrounding the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Mandir intensified on Tuesday after Uttar Pradesh Congress President Ajay Rai was allowed to offer prayers at the Ram Mandir around 9 pm, nearly 20 hours after being placed under house arrest. Police had detained Rai late Monday night to prevent a proposed protest by a Congress delegation over the alleged donation theft. Images of his temple visit had not surfaced at the time of reporting. Ajay Rai detained ahead of planned protest Police placed Ajay Rai under house arrest at an Ayodhya hotel around 11:30 pm on Monday before shifting him to the guest house of Narendra Dev University of Agriculture and Technology, nearly 50 km from the Ram Mandir. Rai was leading a Congress delegation that had announced a protest outside the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust office over the alleged donation theft. The delegation also included Congress MPs Kishori Lal Sharma, Tanuj Punia, and Ujjwal Raman Singh, all of whom were also placed under house arrest. Congress workers detained during March At around 12:30 pm on Tuesday, Congress workers attempted to march towards the Ram Janmabhoomi temple. Police stopped them at Tedhi Bazar, nearly one kilometre from the temple, leading to a confrontation. As workers allegedly tried to push through the barricades, police used mild force and detained several protesters before taking them away in police vehicles. Ajay Rai's wife alleges political vendetta Earlier in the day, Ajay Rai's wife, Reena Rai, released a video statement from Varanasi, accusing the BJP government of trying to suppress her husband's voice. She alleged that after taking him away in a police vehicle, authorities deliberately misled their associates about his whereabouts. Reena Rai also said the Congress would continue its campaign against those allegedly involved in the donation theft and warned that the government would be responsible if any harm came to her husband.

stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is offering a range of subsidised loan schemes to help young entrepreneurs, women, farmers and businesses start or expand their ventures. Under different state and Central government schemes, eligible applicants can access interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh, low-interest agricultural loans, and business finance worth up to ₹1 crore, depending on the category. Here's a detailed look at the schemes, eligibility criteria and benefits. Interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh for young entrepreneurs Under the Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Yojana, eligible young entrepreneurs can obtain an interest-free and collateral-free loan of up to ₹5 lakh to start a business. The first loan, available on the initial application, must be repaid within four years. In addition, the government provides a 10% subsidy on the project cost. For example, if a business project costs ₹10 lakh, the government will contribute up to ₹1 lakh. Entrepreneurs who repay their first loan on time become eligible for a second loan of up to ₹10 lakh. Under this phase, borrowers pay only 3.5% interest for three years on loans of up to ₹7.5 lakh. stories.title: Monsoon stalled at Bihar border for 19 days:Rainfall remains weak; lack of weather system delays showers in UP until July
stories.summary: The wait for the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh is finally expected to end. According to meteorologists, the monsoon is likely to reach Purvanchal and central Uttar Pradesh by July 1-2. Earlier, forecasts had suggested rainfall between June 20 and 25, but the monsoon system originating over the Bay of Bengal remained stalled along the Bihar border for the past 19 days. The absence of a low-pressure area over Uttar Pradesh primarily caused the delay. Weather experts say the monsoon operates through a chain reaction, and this crucial process did not develop as expected. Why did the monsoon get stuck? How a low-pressure system triggers rainfall Monsoon rainfall depends on the formation of a low-pressure area. When intense heat warms the land and surrounding air, the hot air becomes lighter and rises. This creates a low-pressure vacuum near the surface. To fill this vacuum, moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal rush inland. As these cool, humid winds move over the plains, they form rain-bearing clouds and trigger widespread rainfall. What happened this year This year, Uttar Pradesh failed to develop a sufficiently strong low-pressure system to draw the monsoon winds inland. As a result, the moisture-laden winds slowed considerably and remained stalled near the Bihar border instead of advancing into the state. Monsoon stalled, yet rainfall remains poor The monsoon is currently stalled around Motihari (East Champaran) in Bihar and along the Daltonganj line near the Jharkhand-Bihar border. Interestingly, even the districts where the monsoon has stalled have not received significant rainfall. According to the India Meteorological Department, wind patterns began changing on the evening of June 29. Heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds of 50-60 km/h has been forecast across Bihar and Jharkhand, including Motihari and Daltonganj. Meteorologists believe this weather system will push the stalled monsoon forward, allowing it to enter Uttar Pradesh within the next 24 to 48 hours. June rainfall and July-August forecast June recorded a severe rainfall deficit June proved to be exceptionally dry across Uttar Pradesh. A severe rainfall deficit was recorded in 34 districts, with the state's average rainfall about 60% below normal. Eastern Uttar Pradesh Western Uttar Pradesh July and August may also receive below-normal rain According to Skymet's Long Period Average (LPA) forecast, monsoon rainfall across Uttar Pradesh during July and August is expected to remain slightly below normal. Meteorologists say the influence of El Niño is strengthening once again over the Pacific Ocean. Its impact has slowed the movement of monsoon winds across Uttar Pradesh. Overall monsoon rainfall is expected to be around 90% to 94% of the Long Period Average, placing it in the below-normal category. July outlook The first half of July is expected to bring widespread monsoon rainfall across Purvanchal, Central Uttar Pradesh and Western Uttar Pradesh, providing relief after the prolonged delay. However, monsoon activity may weaken slightly during the second half of the month. Overall, July rainfall is expected to remain about 5% below normal. August outlook The monsoon is expected to weaken further during August, with rainfall likely to remain up to 8% below normal. This could prove particularly significant for Kharif crops, especially paddy, which depend heavily on adequate rainfall during this period. Records broken by June's extreme heat Heatwaves in Uttar Pradesh usually last only two to three days during June. This year, however, the delayed arrival of the monsoon resulted in severe heatwave conditions persisting for 10 to 14 days across nearly two-thirds of the state's districts. Normally, heatwave conditions subside around June 20-22 with the arrival of moisture-laden easterly winds. This year, they continued until June 30, leading to two major weather records. 1. Hottest night in 127 years Daytime temperatures in June typically range between 38°C and 40°C. This year, the mercury climbed to 47.6°C, while night-time temperatures reached 30.8°C, around 5°C to 8°C above normal. In Prayagraj, the minimum temperature on the night of June 11-12 reached 34.3°C, breaking a 127-year-old record. The previous highest night temperature, 33.5°C, was recorded in 1898. 2. UP districts among the world's hottest During June, Uttar Pradesh featured three times in global real-time temperature rankings. In the second week of June, 19 Indian cities were listed among the 20 hottest places in the world. Five districts from Uttar Pradesh featured in that list, Banda, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Mirzapur and Fatehpur. Meanwhile, Kanpur recorded maximum temperatures exceeding 47°C on multiple occasions. Why was the heat so severe? Delayed monsoon and absence of weather systems The monsoon reached Kerala four days later than usual before stalling near the Bihar border for nearly 19 days. This prolonged the spell of dry, hot weather by around eight additional days. At the same time, Uttar Pradesh did not experience any significant weather systems capable of triggering pre-monsoon rainfall. Clear skies allowed intense solar radiation to heat the land continuously, while dry westerly winds blowing from the deserts of Rajasthan and Pakistan kept temperatures exceptionally high across the state. Advice for farmers As widespread monsoon rainfall is expected during the first fortnight of July, farmers are advised to complete delayed paddy transplantation by July 15. With below-normal rainfall forecast for August, farmers should not rely entirely on the monsoon. Greater use of tube wells, borewells and canal irrigation is likely to be necessary, increasing the overall cost of cultivation.

stories.title: Bus crashes into trailer on Yamuna Expressway, 4 killed:27 passengers injured, SSP says, 'Conductor was driving the vehicle'
stories.summary: A Volvo bus crashed into the rear of a trailer on the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura at around 3:30 am on Tuesday, leaving four people dead and 27 passengers injured. The impact was so severe that the front section of the bus became lodged nearly eight feet inside the trailer. Several passengers were trapped inside the wreckage, while the body of one young man was left hanging out of a window. The accident took place in the Raya police station area, around 20 km from the Mathura district headquarters. The bus was travelling from Lucknow to Delhi with 65 passengers on board. Passengers rescued after windows and doors were broken open The collision triggered panic and chaos at the scene. Passengers were rescued by breaking open the bus windows and doors. Police, assisted by local residents, immediately launched a rescue operation. According to officials, 34 passengers escaped unhurt and were later sent to their destinations on other buses. Driver, conductor, cleaner and 1 passenger killed Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shlok Kumar said the victims included- The identities of three of the deceased have not yet been established. Rescue operation lasted nearly two hours Most passengers were asleep when the crash occurred. The force of the impact threw several people between the seats, leaving them trapped inside the mangled bus. Rescue teams used gas cutters to cut through the vehicle and free the trapped passengers. The rescue operation continued for nearly two hours. SSP Shlok Kumar said- Preliminary investigation suggests that the regular driver was not behind the wheel at the time of the accident. Instead, the conductor was driving the bus. The bus was travelling at high speed while the trailer was in its own lane. The conductor suddenly swerved the bus, causing it to crash into the rear of the trailer. See photos- How the accident unfolded ? SP (Rural) Suresh Chandra Rawat said the accident took place around 2 km before the Raya cut on the Yamuna Expressway. A trailer loaded with gravel (registration number RJ 47 GA 8143) was travelling in its designated lane when a speeding Gola Bus Service Volvo coach (registration number BR 28P 4723) approached from behind, lost control and rammed into it. The collision was so forceful that the front of the coach was crushed by 2 to 2.5 metres (around 8 feet). Police received information about the crash at 3:35 am, following which eight Police Response Vehicles (PRVs) and 12 ambulances were dispatched to the scene. A green corridor was created to ensure the injured could be transported to hospital without delay. SP Rawat said all the injured are receiving treatment and their condition is currently stable. The preliminary investigation indicates that driver negligence and overspeeding were the primary causes of the accident. Passengers escaped through the emergency exit Preeti Srivastava, a resident of Faridabad, said she was travelling from Lucknow to Faridabad with her husband and two children. She said the coach was travelling at a high speed and had stopped at a roadside eatery about 30 minutes before the accident. Shortly after resuming the journey, the vehicle began swerving. Many passengers were asleep when the crash occurred. "The passengers were thrown from their seats. People broke the glass of the emergency exit at the rear of the coach to rescue those trapped inside. We were later taken to hospital by ambulance," she said. Some injured referred to Agra, three in serious condition Dr Sushil Kumar of the Mathura District Hospital said 24 injured passengers had been brought to the hospital following the accident. Some of the injured have been referred to Agra for specialised treatment, while others from Delhi are also being transferred for further medical care. He said two to three patients remain in a serious condition, suffering fractures to the thigh bone (femur). The condition of the remaining injured passengers is stable.

stories.title: Why UP BJP took 6 months to form new team?:Two key reasons emerge as party plays OBC card against PDA; Yogi kept distance
stories.summary: BJP's state executive's new team was announced 6 months late. More than 50% new faces have been given responsibility, sidelining those who had been in their positions for a long time. Now, preparations are underway to promote big faces. BJP wants to reduce the 'pressure politics' of its coalition partners. This is why, despite the alliance with RLD in the west, Gurjar and Jat leaders were given preference. The same was done with Rajbhar and Maurya faces in Purvanchal. 25 office bearers are from the OBC category alone. Along with the announcement of the list, there is also a discussion in political circles that CM Yogi did not intervene much. First, let's understand how this list got delayed by 6 months According to party sources, there was a long tug-of-war between the central and state leadership in finalizing the list. Two reasons emerged for this- Conflict over Yuva Morcha - There was a tough competition between Nikhil Mani Tiwari, Harshvardhan Singh, and Rohit Mishra for the post of Yuva Morcha's regional president. Different powerful leaders within the party were lobbying for all three. There was also constant opposition among them. This is why it took time to reach a consensus on one name. Finally, Rohit Mishra's name was finalized. Rohit was previously serving as the Vice President in Yuva Morcha. Kashi Region's Complication - The name of Kashi's regional president is decided directly with the consent of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This is why it took a long time for this post to be finalized. Yogi maintained distance, Dharmpal-Pankaj Chaudhary's preferences dominated The biggest political signal was that CM Yogi did not interfere at all in the functioning and appointments of the organization. Most of the names in the entire list were included based on the preferences of General Secretary (Organization) Dharmpal Singh and State President Pankaj Chaudhary. The coordination between him and Dharmpal Singh can be seen as 'Delhi-Lucknow tuning'. The only leader in this team considered close to the Chief Minister is Kameshwar Singh, who has been made the state vice-president. However, experts say that Kameshwar has been the state president of the Kisan Morcha. This is why his selection is considered appropriate. Veterans removed, some to be promoted Many big wickets have also fallen in this reshuffle. Veteran leaders like Vice Presidents Triyambak Tripathi, Santosh Singh, and Vijay Bahadur Pathak have been removed from the state team. This is giving many big signals in the state's politics. It is being discussed that even though Amar Pal Maurya and Govind Shukla, who were removed from the post of state general secretary, may not have got a place in the UP team. But, they can be given a big responsibility in the central team of BJP National President Nitin Naveen. Therefore, taking these powerful general secretaries from UP to the center shows that they are being 'promoted' instead of being 'angered'. This is an exercise to maintain the upper caste and Maurya (OBC) equation at the national level. 'Perform or Go Out' message The changes are like a major surgery for the organization, which was accused of sluggishness after the Lok Sabha election results. Bringing in more than 50% new faces by removing long-serving leaders proves that the party has given a 'perform or go out' message. This is to infuse new enthusiasm among grassroots workers before the 2027 assembly elections. BJP's 'OBC Card' against PDA The party has paid special attention to social engineering this time. In this 54-member team, 27 office bearers have been made from the OBC category. Here too, balance has been achieved by giving representation not to a single caste, but to all major castes falling under OBC. Political analysts believe that a similar trend was seen during the expansion of the Yogi cabinet. Now, backward classes have been given importance in the organization as well. This message could prove to be a game-changer for BJP in the 2027 elections. Political equations balanced for 2027 Countering SP's 'PDA' Narrative - BJP has included 21 Savarna (upper caste), 25 OBC, 7 Dalit, and 1 ST. An attempt has been made to completely break the casteist narrative. At the same time, efforts have been made to address the dissatisfaction of the Savarnas. Reduced Dependence on Alliance Partners - BJP has an alliance with RLD in the West, and with SBSP and Apna Dal in Purvanchal. Despite this, prominent positions have been given to Gurjar, Rajbhar, Maurya, and Chauhan leaders in the organization. This shows that BJP does not want its independent vote bank to weaken. 16 Faces included from Purvanchal In Pankaj Chaudhary's team, 16 office-bearers are from Purvanchal (Gorakhpur and Kashi regions). From Gorakhpur are State Vice President Dharmendra Rai, State Vice President Kameshwar Singh, and Ramesh Singh. Meanwhile, there are 9 office-bearers from the West. There are 10 office-bearers from Awadh region, 8 from Braj, and 3 from Kanpur region. Out of the 6 state presidents of frontal organizations, 4 frontal organizations' state presidents are from Purvanchal. Rohit Mishra, the State President of Yuva Morcha (Youth Front), is also from Pratapgarh, Purvanchal. Devendra Singh, the State President of Kisan Morcha (Farmers' Front), is from Azamgarh. Saroj Kushwah, the State President of Mahila Morcha (Women's Front), is from Ghazipur, and Vidya Bhushan Gond, the State President of ST Morcha (ST Front), is also from Varanasi.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan Singh receives death threat:Youth writes, 'Will shoot him openly and bring the entire system down'
stories.summary: Former BJP MP Brijbhushan Sharan Singh received a death threat on Thursday evening after a threatening post was shared on Facebook by a person identified as Pandit Shankar Dutt Shukla. The post, uploaded around 6:30 pm, warned of targeting the former MP and made violent remarks against the system. In the post, Shukla claimed that he always carries out what he says and wrote that the entire system would be set on fire. He also stated that Brijbhushan Sharan Singh would be openly targeted. Following a complaint, Gonda Police launched an investigation into the matter. Brijbhushan Sharan Singh is a former BJP MP from the Kaiserganj constituency. The person who issued the threat identified himself as a BJP leader The youth who threatened on Facebook has identified himself as a youth leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party. His Facebook profile shows his residence as Ayodhya. This post was made at 6:30 PM. Kaiserganj MP representative Sanjeev Singh has filed a complaint regarding this. Sanjeev Singh stated that he received a Facebook post. In it, Pandit Shankar Dutt Shukla has threatened to 'target' Brijbhushan Sharan Singh. A complaint has been filed with the police demanding strict action against the person who issued the threat. City Kotwal Bindeshwari Mani Tripathi stated that no complaint letter has been received by them yet. Strict action will be taken once the letter is received. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Shankar Dutt Shukla, who allegedly issued the threat. Read the conversation… What did you write to Brij Bhushan Singh? I wrote what I felt was right to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. Why shouldn't I? During the Ram Temple movement, my grandfather supported him. He also stood alongside Atalji. I am going through a difficult situation and believed that my issue would be resolved through Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. However, he did not answer a single one of my calls. When one of his aides answered, he said, "Netaji is not available." Is that the way to respond to someone? My grandfather's name is Ram Kuber Shukla. I am a resident of Gilauli village in the Itiyathok police station area. Why did you write on Facebook that "we will shoot him"? I was angry, so I posted it on Facebook. I had been trying to contact him for nearly two months, hoping my issue would be resolved. It was related to a land dispute. Yes, I wrote the post myself. I am facing some personal difficulties, which is why I kept calling him. I have no personal enmity with Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, nor do I actually want to shoot him. Did someone ask you to post it on Facebook, or did you write it yourself? It is a personal matter. Either he should shoot me, or I will shoot him—that is what I wrote in anger. When ordinary people are not heard, what are they supposed to do? Please convey my message to him. If I cannot meet him, then let him shoot me instead. Please make sure Brij Bhushan Singh is informed about the situation. Anyway, I made a mistake. I admit it and apologise. Threats received before It was June 14. Brijbhushan's son and BJP MLA Prateek Bhushan was on a tour of the area. At 2:22 PM, he received a call on his mobile from an unknown number. stories.title: FIR filed in Ram Mandir donation theft case:Tinnu Yadav among 8 named; top trust officials left out
stories.summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on Thursday lodged an FIR in connection with the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir. Eight people have been named as accused in the case. As many as 3 people have been arrested as well. The complaint was filed by trust member Krishna Mohan based on the preliminary findings of the Special Investigation Team (SIT). The SIT was constituted on 13 June to probe the allegations and submitted its report to the Uttar Pradesh government on 23 June. Those named in the FIR include Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, driver to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, along with Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla, Manish Yadav, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Chandra Srivastava and Karunesh Pandey. Champat Rai's name does not figure in the FIR. Earlier in the day, AAP MP Sanjay Singh submitted 11 documents related to the alleged land scam linked to the temple to the SIT. He met SIT chairman Vijay Vishwas Pant at his Lucknow office and handed over the documents. Speaking to reporters afterwards, Singh claimed that evidence of both financial irregularities and theft of offerings had already surfaced. He questioned why no arrests had been made and why an FIR had not been registered earlier despite the findings. “One revelation after another is coming to light. Cash recoveries have already been made and evidence relating to alleged theft from Mandir donations has surfaced. Yet no one has gone to jail so far. Why has nobody been arrested? Why has no FIR been registered? This is extremely surprising,” said Sanjay Singh. Kejriwal alleges SIT Is focusing on junior staff AAP chief and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also reacted to the case, saying he was saddened by the allegations of theft of offerings at the Ram Temple and would visit Ayodhya on Friday to offer prayers. Meanwhile, reports circulating on social media claiming that Trust General Secretary Champat Rai had resigned were dismissed by temple construction in-charge Gopal Rao. He said no resignation had been submitted and urged people not to believe rumours, adding that the SIT investigation was ongoing and the truth would emerge once its report was released. VHP national general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra also rejected the resignation claims. Separately, Kejriwal alleged that the SIT was focusing on lower-level employees while avoiding action against those responsible for the alleged irregularities.

stories.title: From cricketing glory to spiritual bliss:Akash Deep's marriage in Kashi steals spotlight; wedding stage resembled cricket field
stories.summary: On Wednesday, Indian fast bowler Akash Deep began a new chapter of his life in Kashi, exchanging wedding vows with Akshita in a grand ceremony attended by family members, friends and prominent guests. The wedding stage was designed to resemble a cricket ground, reflecting the groom's sporting journey. As he stood beside his bride, Akash Deep appeared visibly delighted, celebrating the occasion with the same enthusiasm he displays on the cricket field. A celebratory moment on stage In a light-hearted moment, Akash Deep raised his bride's hand and flashed a victory sign, symbolising celebration and happiness. As Akshita approached him for the traditional exchange of garlands, he smiled warmly, bowed his head and accepted the garland. The couple then exchanged garlands and greeted guests with folded hands. The ceremony was met with loud applause from those present, while family members showered flower petals on the newlyweds. Prominent guests attend the wedding Several distinguished personalities attended the ceremony to bless the couple. Among them was Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh, who congratulated the bride and groom. Popular songs by Pawan Singh were played during the celebrations, adding to the festive atmosphere. A number of legislators and political leaders from Bihar were also present and extended their best wishes to the newly married couple. Grand wedding procession at Taj Ganges Hotel The wedding procession took place at the Taj Ganges Hotel, where Akash Deep danced enthusiastically alongside relatives and friends. The celebrations featured traditional music, with bands and drums creating a lively atmosphere as guests joined in the festivities. Around 350 people attended the wedding ceremony. Traditional Kashi rituals performed Scholars and priests from Kashi conducted the traditional 'Dwar Puja' along with special religious rituals. Following the blowing of conch shells on the stage, which was decorated around themes inspired by Kashi and Lord Shiva, chants of- Namah Parvati Pataye, Har Har Mahadev echoed throughout the venue. Venue decorated in Kashi and Shiva theme The wedding venue reflected the spiritual and cultural heritage of Kashi. From the entrance to the stage and dining area, decorations featured symbols associated with Lord Shiva and Hindu tradition, including- Elements of Kashi's culture and Indian traditions were visible throughout the venue, creating a distinctly spiritual and cultural ambience for the occasion. Air India launches ‘Easy Connect’ service from Varanasi:Aviation minister Rammohan Naidu inaugurates new link to connecting flights across 17 countries
stories.summary: Air India's 'Easy Connect' service was launched on Thursday at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi. Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu inaugurated the service following a traditional puja ceremony. The initiative is expected to make international travel significantly easier for passengers from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities such as Varanasi, Lucknow and Patna by providing seamless connections through Delhi. The service has been introduced under the Central Government's 'Hub and Spoke' aviation model. Easier access to International destinations Under the new system, passengers travelling from Varanasi to Delhi will benefit from improved connectivity to international destinations across 17 countries. These destinations include regions such as- The service is designed to provide smoother transfers and reduce the complexities typically associated with connecting international flights. Strengthening India's global air connectivity Speaking at the launch, Union Civil Aviation Minister Rammohan Naidu Kinjarapu described the initiative as an important step towards enhancing India's global aviation connectivity. He said the service would contribute significantly to the government's objective of developing India into an international aviation hub, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision. According to the minister, passengers, traders, students and tourists from the Purvanchal region will particularly benefit from the improved connectivity. International travel through the Delhi hub is expected to become more convenient, while access to onward connecting flights will also improve. New boost for Purvanchal's Aviation Network Air India Station Manager Atif Idris said the Hub and Spoke model links regional cities with major aviation centres, allowing passengers to access a broader international network. According to him, the model offers- Airport Director Puneet Gupta said the initiative would strengthen air connectivity across Purvanchal and support the growth of tourism, trade and investment in the region. Senior officials attend launch event The launch programme was attended by several senior officials, including- How the hub and spoke model work? Officials said the model will be rolled out in phases across several other cities in the country. The objective is to create a more efficient, integrated and globally competitive aviation ecosystem. Under the Hub and Spoke model- Passengers from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities can complete check-in procedures for their final international destination directly at their departure airport. No need to re-check baggage at Delhi One of the key benefits of the Easy Connect service is that passengers will not need to collect and re-check their baggage at the hub airport. After arriving in Delhi, travellers can seamlessly connect to Air India's extensive international network without additional baggage formalities. Immigration clearance at the origin Airport Another major advantage is that passengers will complete their international immigration procedures at their originating airport. This means travellers will- Officials also noted that passengers will no longer face the inconvenience and unfamiliarity often associated with transiting through foreign hub airports before reaching their final destinations. The initiative is expected to make international travel simpler, faster and more accessible for passengers from regional cities across northern and eastern India.

stories.title: BHU-UG admissions to begin from the first week of July:New courses will be launched, NTA to share list of qualified students with BHU
stories.summary: Amidst the PG admission process at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), the National Testing Agency (NTA) has declared the CUET-UG 2025 results. Following this, the central admission committee has also started preparations for undergraduate (UG) admissions. It is expected that after receiving the list of qualified candidates from NTA in the next one week, the UG admission process will be started from the first week of July. In 2024, approximately 8,889 students took admission in BHU. In the last session, two new courses like BSc Radiotherapy and Radiology were introduced, and the number of seats had gone up. At the same time, seats were reduced in some courses with low demand, and new courses were also started in affiliated colleges. Last year, the university had planned admissions for about 9,200 seats, but due to delays in the admission process, many seats remained vacant. This time, the university is set to complete the admission process in a time-bound manner. Admission counseling announced 10-15 days after receiving data This year, due to the timely start of the admission process, all seats are expected to be filled. Along with the implementation of CBCS (Choice Based Credit System) since last year, BHU will also admit 15% of students in its undergraduate (research) programs. Admission Cell Coordinator Prof. Bhaskar Bhattacharya informed that technical preparations related to admissions have been completed on the BHU website. As soon as the candidates' data is received, the dates for admission counseling will be announced. This may take 10 to 15 days. 1182 paid seats will also be available in the faculties There are more than 9200 seats in undergraduate courses across various faculties, the campus-based women's college, and affiliated colleges. Approximately eight thousand regular seats are available among these. These include 3480 in the main campus, 695 in the women's college, and 3537 seats in affiliated colleges. Additionally, students will also get an opportunity for admission on 1182 paid seats.

stories.title: Climate change could transform Tamil Nadu’s Western Ghats by 2050 | Focus Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The Western Ghats may still be green in the coming decades—but they may not be the same forests we know today. A new study by researchers from Anna University’s Centre for Climate Change and Disaster Management warns that climate change could gradually alter the composition of forests across Tamil Nadu’s Western Ghats, including the Nilgiris, Kodaikanal, Valparai, Courtallam and Kanyakumari regions. The study suggests that evergreen and deciduous forests could shrink, while drier thorn forests may expand by 2050. Such changes could affect biodiversity, water security, carbon storage and ecosystem stability across the State. In this episode of The Hindu Focus Tamil Nadu, D. Suresh Kumar explains what the findings mean, why scientists are concerned, and what the future could hold for one of India’s most important biodiversity hotspots.

stories.title: Coaching centres remain shut in Gorakhpur:Operators missing after safety inspections begin, serious lapses exposed
stories.summary: Following the devastating fire incident in Lucknow, authorities have launched inspections of safety arrangements at coaching centres across Uttar Pradesh. The impact of the crackdown is clearly visible in Gorakhpur, where many coaching institutes have remained closed for the third consecutive day. Centres that would normally be filled with hundreds of students attending classes now stand deserted. Several coaching operators have apparently chosen to shut their centres rather than face inspection. Attempts to contact them proved unsuccessful, with many mobile phones switched off and some operators declining to answer calls. This has raised an important question: why did so many coaching centres close immediately after the inspections began? Are operators trying to hide safety deficiencies? The closure of coaching centres during the inspection drive has led to concerns that some institutions may be attempting to conceal shortcomings in fire safety measures, emergency exits and other essential safety standards. To examine these concerns, the Bhaskar team conducted a ground investigation of coaching centres operating in different parts of Gorakhpur. The inspection uncovered serious safety concerns at several locations. Many centres were found operating in buildings accessed through narrow lanes and cramped staircases, potentially making safe evacuation extremely difficult during an emergency. Buddha Coaching Centre found closed When the Bhaskar team visited Buddha Coaching Centre in Hariom Nagar, the main entrance was locked. A premises that is usually crowded with students was completely empty. Efforts to contact the operator were unsuccessful, as the registered mobile number was switched off. The on-site inspection revealed that the coaching centre operates from a two-storey building and caters to approximately 50 to 60 students daily. However, the available safety arrangements appeared inadequate for the number of students attending classes. Investigators found- The most significant concern was the absence of an alternative escape route. In the event of a fire, if smoke filled the staircase or the passage became blocked, students could face serious difficulties evacuating safely. Acme Computer Education also found locked The Bhaskar team then visited Acme Computer Education in Shahi Market. This centre was also found closed, with the main gate locked. Investigators observed that the institute operates from a building accessed through narrow and confined staircases. These stairs serve as the only route for students to enter and leave the premises. In an emergency situation, this could pose a significant risk to evacuation efforts. Safety equipment not visible Around 30 students reportedly attend classes at the centre every day. Despite this, investigators did not observe- In the event of an accident, the absence of such measures could hamper rescue and relief operations. Student says closure notice gave no reason A student who arrived outside the coaching centre said she had received a message three days earlier informing her that classes would remain suspended for two days. However, no reason for the closure was provided. According to the student, she returned on the third day expecting classes to resume, only to find the centre still closed and the gates locked. Why were centres closed as soon as inspections began? Bhaskar's investigation found that several other coaching centres across the city were in a similar situation. Many institutes reportedly shut down shortly after the inspection campaign was launched. Attempts were made to contact multiple operators, but no responses were received. As a result, questions are being raised over whether institutions that fully comply with safety norms would have any reason to suspend operations during the inspection process. Risks of ignoring student safety Every day, hundreds of students attend coaching centres in pursuit of their academic goals. Parents entrust these institutions with the safety and well-being of their children. However, if coaching centres lack fundamental safety measures such as- Even a minor incident could potentially escalate into a major tragedy. Lessons from the Lucknow fire The situation emerging in Gorakhpur in the aftermath of the Lucknow fire has highlighted concerns about safety standards at educational institutions. The findings suggest that safety measures should exist not merely on paper but in practice. While administrative inspections continue, coaching centre operators are also being urged to place student safety at the centre of their operations and ensure compliance with all required safety norms.

stories.title: LDA seals Bhumi IAS among other coaching centres:Action over fire safety violations after Lucknow blaze killed 15
stories.summary: Following the death of 15 people in the Aliganj fire tragedy, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has launched inspections of coaching centres, libraries and shopping complexes across the city. A joint team of the LDA, Fire Department and police is inspecting establishments operating in violation of safety norms. The team sealed Bhumi IAS Coaching, Vidya Mandir Coaching and Drishtikon Library in Gomti Nagar after finding that they did not meet the required standards. The drive, launched on the instructions of LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar, will continue for the next three weeks. Coaching centres, libraries, hotels, nursing homes, dance studios, playgroup schools and commercial complexes will be inspected. LDA officials said establishments found violating fire safety, parking and building plan norms will face immediate sealing and notice action. On Wednesday alone, 71 establishments were sealed for ignoring safety standards. These included major coaching institutes such as Allen, Gravity, Aakash, Government Exam Wala and Paramount. The LDA also issued notices to 83 building owners. See pictures related to the action Action linked to the fire tragedy A fire had broken out on June 22 in a building in Aliganj. The basement, ground floor and first floor housed a pet shop and clinic. The second floor accommodated Learning Space Library and Head Hopper Studio, which works in 3D art production and game asset outsourcing. Fifteen people working at Head Hopper Studio lost their lives in the blaze. ‘Building should be demolished without a minute’s delay’ Ram Kumar, a resident of Sitapur Road, visited the burnt building on Thursday afternoon. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he said the tragedy was the result of government failure and official negligence. He added that had authorities acted earlier, such an incident could have been prevented. Building owners asking coaching centres to vacate Shiv Kumar Khatri of Gomti Nagar said Bhumi IAS Coaching was operating from his premises and that he had asked it to vacate two days ago. People stopping to see the burnt building The building where 15 people died has now been sealed by police. Residents and passersby continue to stop and look at the structure. Trends outlet told to vacate Officials directed the Trends outlet in Viraj Khand to vacate the premises, stating that the building had not been constructed according to approved standards. Drishtikon Library sealed in Virat Khand The LDA sealed Drishtikon Library in Virat Khand. Officials said the library was being operated from a residential property without fire safety arrangements, and commercial activities were being carried out in a residential complex. Bhumi IAS Coaching sealed in Gomti Nagar The LDA sealed Bhumi IAS Coaching Centre in Gomti Nagar, citing congested classrooms, the absence of a fire exit and a very narrow access route to the coaching centre. Vidya Mandir Coaching sealed in Viraj Khand The LDA also sealed Vidya Mandir Coaching in Viraj Khand for failing to comply with fire safety norms. Action against 19 engineers and 6 PCS officers LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the building where the fire occurred had received approval for a residential map in 2016, but commercial construction later began on the premises. He said demolition orders issued at the time were subsequently withdrawn, though the reasons remain unclear. Action has now been taken against a total of 19 engineers and six PCS officers, including former Executive Engineers (XENs), Junior Engineers (JEs) and Assistant Engineers (AEs) posted at the time. Three to four of them have already retired. Report sent to PMO Following the Aliganj fire that claimed 15 lives and injured several others, the matter is being monitored at the highest level. The state government has sent a detailed report to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), covering rescue and relief operations, compensation for victims, FIRs, arrests, suspension of officials and the SIT investigation. The report also includes details about the causes of the incident, lapses found during the preliminary inquiry, the building’s approval and fire safety status, administrative and legal action taken so far, and measures proposed to prevent similar tragedies in future.

stories.title: Sanjay Singh submits Ram Mandir land scam evidence to SIT:AAP MP hands over 11 papers, questions delay in FIR; Kejriwal to visit Ayodhya tomorrow
stories.summary: AAP MP Sanjay Singh on Thursday submitted documents related to alleged land deal irregularities to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation and land purchase controversy. Singh arrived at the office of SIT Chairman Vijay Vishwas Pant in Lucknow at around 11 am and remained inside for approximately 12 minutes before handing over the documents. Sanjay Singh questions lack of arrests and FIRs Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Sanjay Singh said he had submitted 11 documents that, according to him, contain evidence linked to alleged irregularities in land transactions associated with the Ram Mandir Trust. He said- One revelation after another is coming to light. Cash recoveries have already been made and evidence relating to alleged theft from Mandir donations has surfaced. Yet no one has gone to jail so far. Why has nobody been arrested? Why has no FIR been registered? This is extremely surprising. The SIT had invited Singh to present the evidence after he publicly claimed to possess documents related to the alleged land scam. 'No route left for anyone to escape': Sanjay Singh Sanjay Singh said he had submitted original documents to the SIT and claimed that the evidence leaves little room for those involved to avoid scrutiny. According to Singh, the documents relate to the following transactions- 1. Land purchased by Trust at higher price- The Trust allegedly purchased land worth ₹4.97 crore from Harish and Kusum Pathak for ₹8 crore. Singh claimed that the witnesses to the transaction included Rishi Kumar Upadhyay and Anil Mishra. Anil Mishra is a Trust member, while Rishi Kumar Upadhyay was the BJP mayor at the time. 2. Land resold to Trust within five minutes According to Singh, in 2021 Sultan Ansari and Ravi Mohan Tiwari purchased land from Harish and Kusum Pathak and sold it to the Trust for ₹18.5 crore just five minutes later. He alleged that Anil Mishra and Rishi Kumar Upadhyay were witnesses in both transactions. 3. ₹41.60 lakh land sold for ₹2 crore- Singh alleged that a parcel of land valued at ₹41.60 lakh was sold for ₹2 crore. 4. Land bought by Rishi Upadhyay's nephew- According to Singh, Rishi Kumar Upadhyay's nephew purchased land for ₹20 lakh and sold it seven months later to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. 5. Donated land later sold for ₹1 crore- Singh alleged that on 14 May 2020, Deep Narayan, a nephew of Rishi Kumar Upadhyay, received a piece of land as a donation and later sold it to Champat Rai for ₹1 crore. 6. Land purchased from Braj Mohan Das- According to the documents cited by Singh, on 20 May 2021, Champat Rai purchased land from Braj Mohan Das for ₹5.60 crore, although its earlier valuation was ₹92.50 lakh. 7. Land valued at ₹51.80 lakh- Singh alleged that another parcel of land valued at ₹51.80 lakh was also purchased by Champat Rai, though the final sale amount remains unclear. 8. Land valued at ₹45 lakh- He further claimed that details regarding the sale price of a ₹45 lakh land parcel remain unavailable and require investigation. 9. ₹9 crore land purchased for ₹55.47 crore- According to Singh, a land parcel worth ₹9 crore was purchased on 16 November 2023 for ₹55.47 crore. 10. ₹2.92 crore land sold for ₹24 crore- Singh alleged that on 2 April 2024, land valued at ₹2.92 crore was sold to Champat Rai for ₹24 crore. 11. Nazul land transaction questioned- Referring to official records, Singh claimed that the Ayodhya SDM had identified one of the properties as Nazul land. He questioned how such land could have been purchased for ₹24 crore and alleged that the transaction amounted to a direct misuse of donation funds collected by the Trust. Mandir Trust rejects reports of Champat Rai's resignation Meanwhile, Ram Mandir Construction In-Charge Gopal Rao dismissed reports circulating on social media that Trust General Secretary Champat Rai had resigned. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Rao said- False and misleading information is being spread on social media. People should not pay attention to rumours. The matter is being investigated by the SIT. Wait for the SIT report. The truth will become clear after that. The clarification came after several journalists and social media influencers posted claims on X on Thursday morning suggesting that Champat Rai had stepped down. Dainik Bhaskar subsequently contacted Gopal Rao and VHP National General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra, both of whom denied the reports. Bajrang Lal Bagra also stated that claims regarding Champat Rai's resignation were incorrect. Arvind Kejriwal to visit Ayodhya AAP National Convenor and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is scheduled to arrive at Lucknow Airport before travelling to Ayodhya by road. After an overnight stay in Ayodhya, he is expected to visit the Ram Lalla Mandir on 26 June and offer prayers at Hanumangarhi. Kejriwal is also scheduled to meet several saints and religious leaders during the visit. Political observers view the visit as significant in the context of the ongoing controversy surrounding Ram Mandir donations and land transactions, as well as the broader political developments currently unfolding in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: UP BJP announces new state team ahead of assembly elections:Pooja Pal named VP, Rajnath Singh's younger son also inducted
stories.summary: Ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP on Thursday announced its new state team, comprising 64 office-bearers. Of these, 52 leaders have been included in the state executive committee. The appointments include 19 vice-presidents, 19 secretaries, 8 general secretaries and 6 presidents of party wings. In addition, the party has appointed 6 regional presidents, 3 office secretaries and 3 other office-bearers. Pooja Pal and Neeraj Singh included in state team MLA Pooja Pal, who had rebelled against the Samajwadi Party (SP), has been appointed as a state vice-president. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's younger son, Neeraj Singh, has also been inducted into the state team and appointed as a vice-president. Meanwhile, Rohit Mishra from Pratapgarh has been named president of the BJP Yuva Morcha. State Leadership Team Now Numbers 54 With Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh included, the state leadership team now consists of 54 members. The newly announced team includes 13 women. OBC representation sees significant increase Compared with the previous state executive, representation from the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category has increased substantially. The number of OBC leaders in the state team has risen from 16 to 25. Meanwhile, 21 members from the general category have been included in the new executive. Caste-wise representation in the new team The composition of the state team reflects changes across several communities. Thakur representation has reduced from 7 to 6 members. Brahmin representation has reduced from 8 to 7 members. Four Bhumihar leaders have been included. Three Vaishya leaders have been given positions. One Srivastava representative has been included. SC and ST representation Among Scheduled Caste (SC) communities, seven leaders have been included in the new state team. For Scheduled Tribe (ST) representation, Engineer Vidyabhushan Gond is the sole member to have been appointed. See full list- All six regional presidents replaced The BJP has replaced all six regional presidents across Uttar Pradesh. The new appointments are- Several outgoing regional presidents have been given new responsibilities. Former Kashi regional president Dilip Patel has been promoted and appointed state general secretary. Former Kanpur regional president Prakash Pal has been appointed state president of the BJP OBC Morcha. Former Braj regional president Dhruv Vijay Shakya has been made a state vice-president. Former Gorakhpur regional president Sahajanand Rai has been appointed a state secretary. However, former Western regional president Satyendra Sisodia and former Awadh regional president Kamlesh Mishra have not been included in the new team. Key promotions in the new team Several leaders have been elevated to higher organisational positions. Abhijat Mishra has been promoted from state secretary to state general secretary. Archana Mishra has been elevated from state secretary to state vice-president. Geeta Shakya has been promoted from Mahila Morcha state president to BJP state general secretary. Shankar Lodhi has been elevated from state secretary to state general secretary. Dilip Patel has also been appointed state general secretary following his tenure as Kashi regional president. Why is the new team significant? The new team led by Pankaj Chaudhary will shoulder full responsibility for the BJP's preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. It will also be the first Assembly election in Uttar Pradesh under the supervision of Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh. While he has prior experience handling elections in Jharkhand, this will be his first Uttar Pradesh Assembly poll in the role. The newly constituted team will be responsible for- The team will also be tasked with implementing decisions taken by the BJP's central and state leadership at the grassroots level. Political observers say that during an election year, the role of a state office-bearer carries significance comparable to that of a minister. This is one of the key reasons many former office-bearers were keen to retain their positions in the organisation.

stories.title: Lucknow fire survivor left paralysed after jumping from building:Legs numb, ribs fractured and lungs damaged; 7 doctors fight to save him
stories.summary: Jayant Gupta, who jumped from the second floor of a building to save his life during the Lucknow fire tragedy, has been fighting for survival for the past four days. A severe spinal cord injury has left the lower half of his body numb. Jayant is undergoing treatment at King George's Medical University (KGMU), where specialists from seven departments are monitoring his condition. Severe spinal cord injury leaves legs paralysed Dr Avdhesh Yadav, a neurosurgery expert at KGMU, told Dainik Bhaskar that the road to recovery will be extremely challenging for Jayant. According to Dr Yadav- 'Jayant has fractures in both legs. His legs have become paralysed and are completely numb. This is known as a complete cord injury. The chances of recovery are very low. It remains to be seen how much improvement occurs over time.' However, the doctor expressed hope that Jayant may eventually be able to stand on his own feet again. Jayant fell directly onto an iron grille after jumping from the building. He sustained critical injuries and lost consciousness before being rushed to KGMU's Trauma Centre. See in 3 pictures how Jayant saved his life- Rib fractures and lung injuries detected Doctors said Jayant suffered multiple rib fractures. The 10th rib on the right side and the 9th rib on the left side were severely damaged, causing injuries to his lungs as well. As a result, he has been provided ICD support (Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator) and remains under observation in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Both of his hands were also badly burnt during the incident. A severe injury at the D-10 level of the spinal cord has resulted in paraplegia. Doctors also found blood accumulation around both lungs (bilateral haemothorax) along with multiple rib fractures. He was in a state of shock when admitted to hospital. MRI reveals extensive damage An MRI scan revealed a serious ligament injury in the spine between the D-9 and D-11 vertebral levels. Doctors also detected- Dr Yadav said a multidisciplinary panel of experts has been formed to oversee Jayant's treatment. The team includes specialists from- Experts from other departments will also be consulted if required. Doctors say their primary goal is to ensure Jayant receives the best possible care and recovers as quickly as possible. Treatment provided so far According to hospital officials, Jayant is receiving comprehensive medical care, including oxygen support and broad-spectrum antibiotics. Doctors have conducted- Meanwhile, the plastic surgery team is treating his burn injuries. Conscious and stable in ICU Doctors said Jayant is fully conscious and responding appropriately to medical instructions. His blood pressure and other vital parameters remain stable. He is breathing normally without assistance and does not require ventilator support. His oxygen saturation level has been recorded at 96 per cent while breathing room air. A talented animation artist Jayant had been working at Head Hopper Studio since June 2022. Over the years, he developed expertise in hard-surface 3D modelling and texturing. More recently, he had focused on character modelling for animation projects. He learned animation at MAAC India and created several notable 3D character designs, including Textured Carbine and Wonder Woman. Key facts about Jayant Jump that saved his life Jayant was working on the second floor of Head Hopper Studio when the fire broke out. As flames engulfed the building and escape routes became inaccessible, he jumped from the second floor in an attempt to save himself. He landed on an iron grille and sustained life-threatening injuries. Although he survived the blaze, all 15 people who remained trapped inside the building lost their lives.

stories.title: Suspected Ram Mandir attack plot foiled:UP man arrested in Karnataka; ATS claims links to Pakistan-based terror group
stories.summary: A suspected terrorist allegedly plotting to blow up the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was arrested by the ATS and NIA in Karnataka on Wednesday evening. The accused, identified as Mohammad Suhail (22), is a resident of Gangoh in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district and was working in a factory in Karnataka. The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) claims that Suhail had links with a Pakistan-based terrorist organisation. Investigators say he had been living in Davangere, Karnataka, while concealing his identity, although the exact manner in which he did so remains unclear. Agencies have reportedly recovered Pakistani phone numbers, suspicious WhatsApp group links, and photographs showing him with weapons from his mobile phone. Officers from the NIA and ATS are currently interrogating him, and he may soon be brought to Uttar Pradesh for further questioning. Lead emerged during interrogation of two suspected terrorists According to sources, ATS recently arrested two suspected terrorists, Zameer Khan (22) from Davangere and Alla Baksh (24) from Tumakuru. During questioning, both allegedly disclosed Suhail's name. Acting on this information, ATS launched an operation and arrested him. Preliminary investigations suggest that Suhail was in contact with Pakistani terrorists through social media platforms. What did investigators find on Suhail's mobile phone? Officials say that during interrogation, Suhail admitted discussing plans to attack the Ram Mandir. Investigating agencies claim to have recovered photographs of him posing with weapons from his mobile phone. These images have been sent for forensic examination. In addition, officers reportedly found phone numbers bearing Pakistan's country code and several audio clips. In some of these recordings, Suhail is allegedly heard discussing plans to target the Ram Mandir. Taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation Davangere Superintendent of Police (SP) Shekhar HT said intelligence agencies had already received inputs regarding Suhail's activities. Following these inputs, a joint operation was carried out by Deputy SP Basavaraj of Davangere Rural Sub-Division, the Central Intelligence Agency, and the Davangere Crime Branch team. Suhail was arrested from Bannikodu village in Davangere district and is being taken to Tumakuru for further interrogation. Suhail's father, Liaqat, said he works as a labourer and has nine children — five daughters and four sons. Suhail is the youngest among all his siblings. All five daughters are married. His eldest brother, Ayaz, works as a driver in Saudi Arabia. The second brother, Shoaib, lives at home and is currently unemployed. The third brother, Jamil, works in the hosiery industry in Delhi. Suhail is the youngest and fourth son in the family. Worked as a labourer before going to Karnataka According to Suhail's father Liaqat, he studied at a madrasa up to Year 5. He previously worked as a daily-wage labourer. On 6 June, he travelled to Karnataka through a contractor to work as a painter. Liaqat claimed that Suhail was "mentally unstable" and had a strong desire to become famous on Instagram. He added- "I do not know what happened after he went to Karnataka. I have no information about his activities there."

stories.title: Sindhi body claims 200 kg silver handed to Champat Rai:No receipt issued yet from Ram Mandir; 'Kakabhushundi' idol also missing
stories.summary: New allegations are surfacing daily in the Shri Ram Temple offerings theft case in Ayodhya. The Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam of Mumbai has claimed it has not received a receipt for the 200 kg of silver it donated, nor has the trust disclosed how the silver was used. A woman has also alleged that she was not given a receipt for donating a silver idol of Kakabhushundi. Both donations were reportedly handed over to Champat Rai, the temple trust’s general secretary. Meanwhile, Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony of the Sheshavatar Temple in the complex on June 23. Their presence has fueled speculation that all three may receive a clean chit in the offerings theft case. Read this report 200 Sindhis from 15 countries had donated silver slabs Dr. Raju Manwani, Chairman of Vishwa Sindhi Seva Sangam, told Dainik Bhaskar that At the time of temple construction, the whole world was donating. The Sindhi community also decided to donate 20-25 kg of silver. However, 200 people from the Sindhi community living in more than 15 countries were ready to donate one kilogram of silver each. After collecting 200 kg of silver bricks, we contacted Champat Rai. He took the bricks and called us to Ayodhya. 200 people from the community reached Ayodhya with the bricks on January 26, 2021. After the worship of the bricks, they were handed over to Champat Rai. Dr. Raju Manwani said, All the bricks had pictures of Lord Jhulelal and other deities. Champat Rai said that after checking the purity of the bricks, a receipt would be sent. He also assured that we would be informed where the bricks would be used.Today it has been five years, but no receipt has been given by the Trust. Neither did anyone call, nor did we receive any response on our phones. After the case of theft of offerings came to light, I have received calls from many people in the community. They want to know where the donated 200 kg of silver has been used. Silver Kakabhushundi idol also missing A woman named Anita Bhardwaj has also accused them of not providing a receipt for donated silver. The woman claims that she gave a silver idol of Kakabhushundi (a sage in the form of a crow) to Champat Rai in Karsevakpuram. She had requested him to give it a place in the Ram Darbar. Champat Rai had said that cameras are not allowed inside. Photos and receipts will be sent later. After this, Anita wrote several letters to Champat Rai asking for the receipt, but she has not received it to date. She was also not told anything about that idol. 5 suspects imprisoned in Ram Mandir complex The initial investigation in the offering theft case was conducted by the Trust itself. It is being claimed that the Trust has seized approximately 2 crore rupees and jewelry from the homes and stated locations of several personnel by June 13. Since then, the suspects Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Avinash, Karunesh, and Manish Yadav have been kept within the temple premises. Their mobile phones have also been confiscated. The SIT has also interrogated them. Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, who was formerly the driver of General Secretary Champat Rai, has also been kept on the premises. However, he is allowed to move freely anywhere within the premises. He is also using a mobile phone. Whereas, Tinnu is still being described as the main figure in the offering theft case. The recovery of jewelry from his house has also come to light. The temple administrators are living in the temple premises as before. Champat Rai is also living in the temple. Earlier, he used to live in the VHP office located in Karsevakpuram. Dr. Anil Mishra is commuting from his home. All three trustees likely to get a clean chit In the offerings theft case, the roles of General Secretary Champat Rai, counting in-charge and trust member Dr Anil Mishra, and manager Gopal Rao are under scrutiny. Former temple accountant Mahipal and former engineer Dinanath Verma have alleged that Champat Rai was aware of both the theft of offerings and a 40% commission in the purchase of construction materials. They claim they informed him, but instead of taking action, both were removed from temple duties. Mumbai businessman Anil Vishwakarma has accused Champat Rai of not issuing receipts for a Dwadash Jyotirling necklace and foot-pads donated to the temple. The SIT has recorded statements from Vishwakarma and Guru Acharya Vinod Mishra, while the Indian Bullion Jewellers Association has also raised questions over 60 kg of silver bricks. During his recent visit to Ayodhya, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reportedly kept all three individuals away from official programmes. However, Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao were seen actively participating in the flag-hoisting ceremony at Sheshavatar Temple on 23 June. Champat Rai led the event and delivered a speech, fuelling claims that all three have received a clean chit in the SIT's preliminary report.

stories.title: Heavy rain in Prayagraj, alert issued for 26 districts:Temperature crosses 44°C, heat and humidity intensify
stories.summary: The spell of fluctuating weather conditions continues across Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rain accompanied by strong winds was reported in Prayagraj early on Thursday, while light drizzle occurred in Meerut. Most cities across the state witnessed bright sunshine from the morning onwards. With wind speeds remaining low, heat and humidity levels have increased significantly. Rain and heatwave alerts issued The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 26 districts and a heatwave warning for eight districts on Thursday. Strong winds with speeds of up to 60 kmph are also likely during this period. Monsoon Expected to Enter UP Within 2–3 Days There is some relief on the monsoon front, with weather officials indicating that the southwest monsoon could enter Uttar Pradesh within the next two to three days. The monsoon is expected to enter the state through the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj region via the Bihar border by 28 June. According to forecasts- Typically, the monsoon reaches Uttar Pradesh by around 20 June. This year, however, it is running approximately eight days behind schedule. The monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj for the past 15 days. Banda records highest temperature During the past 24 hours, Banda was the hottest location in the state, recording a maximum temperature of 44.2°C. Several districts experienced heavy rainfall, including- In Agra, strong winds during the evening caused a roadside utility pole to collapse onto parked cars. The rear portions of two vehicles were crushed in the incident. Lucknow Meteorological Centre scientist Atul Kumar Singh said the southwest monsoon became active over parts of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on June 23. He said the monsoon is expected to advance over the remaining parts of the North Arabian Sea, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand over the next two to three days. This could allow it to reach parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar within the next three to four days. How will the weather for the next five days ? 26 June: Dry weather is expected across eastern and western Uttar Pradesh, with temperatures likely to rise. 27 June: Heatwave conditions are expected to persist across the state. Hot winds may intensify discomfort, especially in eastern Uttar Pradesh. 28 June: Western Uttar Pradesh is likely to remain dry, while eastern districts may receive rain. 29 June: Light rain is likely in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern parts may witness heavy rainfall. 30 June: Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected in western Uttar Pradesh. Eastern Uttar Pradesh may experience strong storms along with widespread rainfall.
