stories.title: Varanasi 8th hottest city in India:41°C temperature recorded; June rainfall remains low at 10%
stories.summary: The severe heatwave continues to grip Purvanchal, with temperatures rising to 40.5°C by Saturday afternoon. Wind speeds of around 8 km/h and humidity levels of 53% were recorded in the region. Meteorologists have predicted that a mild monsoon influence may reach the district within the next 48 hours, which could bring much-needed relief from the intense heat. See 2 pictures BHU's special preparations before monsoon To deal with the problem of potential heavy rainfall and waterlogging, BHU administration has started comprehensive preparations. Powerful pumps are being installed for rainwater drainage in low-lying areas including Sunderlal Hospital, Trauma Center, hostels and residential complexes. With the help of these pumps, rainwater will be quickly drained out so that waterlogging situations do not occur in hospitals and other important complexes. BHU has prepared an action plan in collaboration with Municipal Corporation The university administration has prepared a coordinated action plan in collaboration with the Municipal Corporation and Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam. Under the campaign running since June 6th, work is being carried out at a rapid pace to clean the rainwater drainage network, remove silt from drains, and strengthen the drainage system. The university's construction department, sanitation and support services, and horticulture department are jointly engaged in cleaning all major drains before the monsoon. Within the next two to three days, pumps will be installed in trauma centers and other sensitive areas. Agriculture Department's advice to farmers: cultivate coarse grains In view of the lack of rainfall, District Agriculture Officer Birendra Kumar has advised farmers to remain alert. He informed that this year, due to the effect of El Nio, there has been less than normal rainfall in the month of June and the possibility of good rain ahead also appears low. He said that in areas where there is no adequate irrigation arrangement, farmers should give priority to the cultivation of pulses and millets (coarse grains). Farmers who have irrigation facilities available have been advised to transplant paddy varieties that mature in 100 to 110 days, so that the impact of potential drought is minimized. The Agriculture Department has also appealed to farmers to definitely get crop insurance. Electricity demand at record level The impact of severe heat is clearly visible on electricity consumption as well. In the district, demand for more than 900 megawatts of electricity has been continuously recorded for the past ten days. On June 25, the highest demand of 970 megawatts of electricity was recorded in the district. Electricity demand in the four districts of Varanasi division - Varanasi, Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur - continues to remain at high levels. Due to increasing consumption, pressure on the electricity system has increased.

stories.title: UPTET-2026 to be held in Varanasi:Admit cards to be issued from 30 June; exam scheduled from 2 to 4 July
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission has completed all preparations for UPTET-2026. Under the supervision of Commission Chairman Dr. Prashant Kumar, the examination will be conducted with complete transparency and impartiality across 955 centres in 60 districts of the state, including Varanasi. UPTET-2026 will be held from July 2 to 4 in multiple shifts. On July 2, the Upper Primary Level (Classes 6 to 8) examination will be conducted in both shifts. On July 3, the Upper Primary Level exam will take place in the first shift, while the Primary Level (Classes 1 to 5) exam will be held in the second shift. On July 4, the Primary Level examination will be conducted in the first shift only. The first shift will run from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM, while the second shift will be from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM. The Commission has uploaded detailed information regarding examination districts on its official website https://upessc.up.gov.in from June 22. Candidates can verify their details through the link provided on the website and check their allotted examination district. Admit cards will be available for download from June 30 on the Commission’s website. The Chairman has advised candidates to download their admit cards on time and strictly follow the instructions mentioned. No candidate will be allowed entry to the examination centre without a valid admit card.

stories.title: Mukesh Khanna lashes out on Ram Mandir donation scam:Actor says 'They are worse than thieves, they are robbing God'
stories.summary: Senior actor Mukesh Khanna has lashed out at the donation scam that occurred at the Ram Temple. He says that those who steal in the temple are above thieves, dacoits, or any dishonest person. He has appealed that devotees should stop offering donations to the temple. Mukesh Khanna wrote from his official Instagram account, Do you know, your cash offerings in temples do not reach God. It gets lost somewhere in between. There is widespread looting. There's a saying, 'Loot if you can.' And those who loot are abundant here. I once said, 'Thieves, dacoits, and dishonest people are abundant, yet my country is great.' But what name should I give to these donation looters? Thieves, dacoits, or dishonest people? None of these. Because they are above all of them. They are not only looting devotees but also God.' Further, he wrote, 'I would only advise devotees that if there's no bamboo, there's no flute (meaning, remove the root cause), similarly, if there's no offering, there's no scam. So stop making offerings. Especially money and jewellery. God will be pleased.' What is the whole matter? On June 7, a case of theft of offerings at the Ram Temple came to light. An SIT was formed to investigate the theft of offerings on the orders of the Yogi government. Initial investigations indicated irregularities in matters related to donations, offerings, and management. Based on the SIT report, the police registered an FIR against 8 named accused, arrested and sent them to jail. This made the whole matter serious. Meanwhile, Champat Rai, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Trust, and Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra have resigned. According to sources, Gopal Rao, in charge of temple construction, has also been removed from the temple's management.

stories.title: Yogi says, 'BJP secured Indian borders':UP CM claims before 2014 enemies threatened India; now air and surgical strikes follow
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the BJP Mahanagar's two-day training camp on Saturday. Addressing party workers, he said India's approach to national security has changed significantly since 2014. Yogi said that before 2014, Indian soldiers were subjected to atrocities by enemy countries, but governments hesitated to respond for fear of harming diplomatic relations. "There was a time when relations with other countries were prioritized over national interest. But after 2014, India has shown the capability to look the enemy in the eye. If anyone encroaches on our borders or attacks Indian soldiers, no one can stop us from carrying out air strikes or surgical strikes," he said. He added that the BJP has demonstrated its resolve and capability in securing India's borders before both the country and the world. See pictures… The Chief Minister said Naxalism is now confined to just one or two districts and will soon be eliminated. He also claimed that terrorism in Kashmir and insurgency in the Northeast have been brought to an end. "Development is possible only when there is security. A strong infrastructure accelerates the country's growth," he said.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri emotional over Ram Mandir donation theft:Says, 'Ravan has only changed his form; God will punish the guilty'
stories.summary: Dhirendra Shastri turned emotional over the theft at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. He said, "Ravan still exists—only his form has changed. Ravan had only abducted Mata Janaki, but this theft has robbed the faith and trust of lakhs and crores of devotees." 'God will also punish the accused' Shastri said an FIR has been registered and demanded a thorough investigation. "The truth is the truth, whether people like it or not. Those who stole the offerings will face government punishment, and God will also give them the greatest punishment," he said. Accused spend restless first night in jail According to jail sources, Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu and the seven other accused spent a sleepless first night in Faizabad Jail. They were reportedly discussing the case among themselves and arguing with each other. All eight accused will be produced in court again on Monday.

stories.title: 2 children die in Lucknow Muharram procession:Balcony collapses during refreshment distribution; 8 trapped under debris
stories.summary: During a Muharram procession in Lucknow, two 12-year-old boys died after the balcony of a house collapsed. Eight people, including four children, were trapped under the debris. Police rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared Ali (12) and Arman (12) dead. After initial treatment, the injured were referred to the KGMU Trauma Centre and a 100-bed hospital. According to police, the incident occurred around 10:15 PM on June 26 in the Pakhariya locality of Mohana, under the Itaunja police station area. A Muharram procession was passing through the locality when members of a family, seated on a six-foot-high balcony outside their house, were distributing sharbat to participants. The balcony suddenly gave way, triggering panic as around 10 people were buried under the debris. People in the procession immediately alerted the police and began rescue efforts by removing the rubble. Police and emergency teams soon reached the spot, and the injured were taken to hospital by ambulance. After the situation was brought under control, the Muharram procession was allowed to continue. 3 pictures Now understand entire matter- According to police, Mushtaq (40), who lives in Pakhariya locality, was standing on his house's balcony and distributing sharbat to people participating in the Muharram procession along with his family. In the rush to get sharbat, several people hung from the balcony. Due to this, the balcony collapsed. Many people got trapped underneath it. In the accident, Ali (12) son of Qasim and Arman (12) son of Imran, who were standing below, died. Ajmal (7) son of Zakki, Ziyan (3), Sana (30) wife of Sharif, Mohammad Haseeb (42) son of Safiq and Ziaul (30) son of Hamid were seriously injured. The condition of Rusida daughter of Liyaqat remains critical. Daud (12) and Abdul Wajood (10) son of Shadab were discharged after first aid. It was fortunate that the family standing on top of the balcony received only minor injuries in the accident. Otherwise, the accident could have been much worse. 'My brother-in-law was also injured' Abrar said - Sherbet was being distributed. The crowd had increased. During this, the canopy collapsed. Many people were injured. Among them, my brother-in-law Haseeb was also seriously injured. His treatment is ongoing. Sumaiya said, “I had gone to get sherbet for the children. During this time the canopy fell. My son Jiyan and husband Haseeb were seriously injured.” DCP North Gopal Chaudhary said- 2 children have died due to the collapse of a canopy. 8 people are injured. Treatment of the injured is ongoing.

stories.title: Monsoon likely in two days:Rain, thunderstorm alert in 30 UP districts, temperatures to drop by 8°C
stories.summary: Monsoon continues to elude Uttar Pradesh, with its arrival delayed by nearly two weeks. The southwest monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj on the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar border for the past 15 days. It usually enters the state by June 20, but this year it is now expected to arrive around June 29, nearly eight days behind schedule. Most parts of the state woke up to bright sunshine on Saturday morning. Mild winds kept temperatures slightly lower in the early hours, but the heat is expected to intensify through the day. Several cities are likely to record temperatures above 42°C, while hot winds will add to people's discomfort. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for 30 districts, with lightning expected at isolated places. A heatwave warning remains in place for 22 districts. On Friday, Lakhimpur Kheri was the hottest city in the state at 43.2°C, followed by Banda and Agra (43°C each), Lucknow (42.4°C), Aligarh (42.2°C) and Prayagraj (42°C). The weather department said monsoon showers are likely to begin in Uttar Pradesh within the next two days. Even areas that do not receive rain immediately are expected to witness increased cloud cover. Temperatures are likely to fall by 8–9°C, bringing relief from the scorching heat and heatwave conditions. Widespread rainfall is expected across most parts of the state from June 30. 'Conditions favourable for monsoon to enter UP in two days' Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh of the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said, "The southwest monsoon has remained stalled near Maharajganj for the past 15 days. Conditions are now becoming favourable for its advance into Uttar Pradesh over the next two days. Heatwave conditions will continue in parts of the state today and tomorrow. However, eastern Uttar Pradesh, the Terai region and a few other areas may witness strong winds and light rainfall during this period." Weather forecast for the next five days Rainfall remains uneven across Uttar Pradesh Rainfall has been uneven across the state's 75 districts this June. Thirty-four districts have recorded a large rainfall deficit, while 13 have received below-normal rain. Sixteen districts have reported normal rainfall, four have recorded above-normal rainfall and seven have received significantly more rainfall than usual. Kaushambi has not recorded any rainfall so far this month. Why is the monsoon moving slowly? According to the weather department, the weakening of the jet stream is delaying the advance of the southwest monsoon. Meteorologists expect it to move forward once atmospheric conditions improve. UP may receive 8% below-normal rainfall this season Senior scientist Atul Singh said Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive below-normal rainfall this monsoon season. The state usually records 820–840 mm of rainfall between June and September, but this year it is expected to receive only 754–773 mm, around 8% below normal. El Niño signals raise concern IMD Director General Dr M. Mahapatra said La Niña-like conditions over the Pacific Ocean are fading and signs of El Niño are emerging, which could reduce rainfall this year. Reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere during January–March may also affect the strength of the southwest monsoon. Impact on farming and food prices Below-normal rainfall could affect Uttar Pradesh's economy, agriculture and daily life. Paddy production may decline by up to 20%, while delayed rainfall in June and July could postpone paddy transplantation and reduce the cultivated area. Farmers may have to rely more on tube wells for irrigation, increasing electricity and diesel costs. Lower crop production could push up the prices of cereals, pulses and vegetables. Drought conditions may also deepen in Bundelkhand and parts of south-western Uttar Pradesh, including Jhansi, Mahoba, Lalitpur and Mathura. Last year's monsoon was above normal According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh received an average of 870–900 mm of rainfall during the 2025 monsoon season (June to September), around 10–15% above the long-term average.

stories.title: Eyewitnesses blame delayed fire brigade response in Lucknow blaze:Claim 15 deaths could have been prevented; Bhaskar conducts reality check
stories.summary: Smoke was coming out from parts of the building. We realised people were trapped inside. We broke the windows by throwing stones, and 4-5 people managed to come down. If the fire brigade had arrived on time, around 15 people could have been saved. The fire brigade did not arrive half an hour late, but after nearly an hour. Even if it had reached within 15-20 minutes, the lives of 15 children could have been saved. These allegations were made by eyewitnesses and families of the victims in the Lucknow fire tragedy. Following these claims, a Bhaskar reporter conducted a reality check. The distance between the accident site and the nearest fire station was covered on a scooter at around 3 pm, the same time the fire broke out. According to official records, the fire station received information at 2:27 pm, while the FIR registered at Aliganj police station states that the fire started at 2:30 pm. This report examines the eyewitness accounts, the route between Kapurthala and Indiranagar Fire Station, and the situation at the accident site. Now see the condition of the building- What happened in the fire? A massive fire broke out on June 22 in a two-storey building in Lucknow's Aliganj area after an alleged AC blast. Five people managed to escape by climbing down through pipes and electrical wires. One youth jumped from the building to save himself but suffered paralysis in both legs. The blaze claimed the lives of 15 students who were attending classes at a 3D animation centre on the second floor. On June 23, an SIT and forensic team inspected the building and questioned the injured at KGMU Hospital. After post-mortem examinations, the bodies were handed over to their families. Following the incident, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) ordered the demolition of the building. Reality check: Reporter reached fire station in 20 minutes The nearest fire station to the accident site is Indiranagar Fire Station, about 6.2 km away. Google Maps estimates the journey by car at 18 minutes. To verify the route, the reporter travelled the same distance on a scooter at around 3 pm and reached the fire station in 20 minutes. However, fire engines move differently from two-wheelers. Officials said 19 fire vehicles, including a hydraulic rescue unit, were sent from different fire stations to tackle the blaze. Eyewitnesses speak 'People broke the windows to rescue those trapped' Eyewitness Sahil Joshi said he was passing by on his bike when he saw smoke rising from the building. People started throwing stones to break the windows. Three to four boys climbed down using electrical wires. Many others remained trapped inside. The entire incident lasted around 20-25 minutes. Everyone kept calling the police and fire brigade, but the fire brigade arrived late. 'Fire trucks reached after more than half an hour' Local resident Kamini said she rushed outside after hearing screams. There was panic everywhere. People were breaking the windows with bricks so the smoke could escape. As soon as the glass shattered, some people tried to jump from the building. We wanted to help but could not. The fire trucks also arrived late, more than half an hour after the fire started. 'The fire engine reached after nearly an hour' Renu, sister-in-law of deceased Neelesh, blamed the delay in the fire brigade's arrival for the high death toll. The fire engine did not arrive after half an hour—it came nearly an hour later. If it had reached even 10-20 minutes earlier, many children could have survived. We lost Neelesh because help did not arrive on time. 'The fire brigade always reaches late' Shubham Mishra, who visited the site, claimed delays were common. The biggest negligence is that the fire brigade always reaches late. Two months ago, my shop caught fire and the fire brigade arrived only after everything had burned. Like police vehicles are stationed at major intersections, fire engines should also be kept ready at key locations so they can respond immediately during emergencies.

stories.title: Lucknow property dealer murder case:Accused killed after being cornered in STF encounter
stories.summary: The main shooter in the murder of Lucknow property dealer Sandeep Singh was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) early on Saturday. Police said the accused, Sanjay alias Sanjeev, opened fire with a carbine after the STF surrounded him on Indira Canal Road. The STF retaliated, killing him in the exchange of fire. Sanjeev had been carrying a reward of ₹1 lakh since the murder of Sandeep Singh on May 27. The property dealer was shot dead outside his office in broad daylight while he was talking on his mobile phone. Two bike-borne attackers opened fire on him and fled. Dainik Bhaskar had accessed the exclusive CCTV footage of the incident. How the murder took place On May 27, between 12 pm and 12:30 pm, Sandeep Singh (42) arrived at his office in the PGI police station area with his driver, Pradeep Singh. As he stepped out of his car and walked towards the office, two masked men arrived on a motorcycle. One of the attackers, dressed in a white shirt and blue jeans, ran towards Sandeep and opened fire. The first bullet hit him in the chest, causing him to collapse on the road. The attacker continued firing even after Sandeep fell and finally shot him near the head. The second accused waited on a running Apache motorcycle. After the shooting, the gunman ran back, got on the bike, and both escaped. The rider was wearing a helmet, while the shooter had covered his face with a white cloth. People nearby rushed Sandeep to Apex Trauma Centre, where he died during treatment. Police recovered a 50-second CCTV recording of the attack. CCTV captures the attack Property dealer was from Jaunpur Sandeep Singh was a native of Takari village in Jaunpur district. He lived with his family near Kalindi Park in Vrindavan Yojana, Lucknow. He is survived by his wife, Preeti Singh, an 11-year-old son, Sarthak, and a nine-year-old daughter, CV Singh. His elder brother, Satish Singh, lives in their native village. Sandeep moved to Lucknow in 2008 to live with his uncle, Rajendra Prasad Singh, a government inter college principal. He later entered the real estate business and, around one-and-a-half years ago, opened an office under the name PSS Builders Private Limited in Yadav Complex, Kalli Paschim Bazaar.

stories.title: RSS pressure before Champat Rai's resignation:Haridwar meeting triggered scrutiny, sources say he was told to step down
stories.summary: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned from their posts on Friday amid growing pressure over the alleged Ram Mandir donation theft case. Sources said the developments were set in motion after a Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) meeting held in Haridwar on June 18 and 19. Champat Rai and Gopal Rao from Ayodhya attended the meeting. According to sources, RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale questioned both leaders over allegations related to Ram Mandir donations and sought an explanation regarding alleged irregularities in donation accounts. After the meeting, pressure on Champat Rai reportedly increased, and senior Sangh leaders began distancing themselves from him. Champat Rai kept away during CM Yogi's Ayodhya visit: Sources Sources claimed that during Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's Ayodhya visit on June 19, Champat Rai was kept away from the Chief Minister's official programmes. With pressure continuing to mount, Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra submitted their resignations to Trust president Mahant Nritya Gopal Das on Friday. RSS and VHP leaders reportedly advised him to step down Sources said Champat Rai received calls from RSS and VHP leaders throughout Thursday night. Some leaders reportedly advised him to resign to help contain the controversy. On Friday morning, Champat Rai performed prayers before reaching Mani Ramdas Ji's camp. Dr Anil Mishra was also called there. Around 11 am, both leaders submitted their resignations to the Trust president. FIR filed 18 days after donation theft came to light The alleged theft of offerings at Ram Mandir came to light on June 7. Eighteen days later, police registered an FIR against eight people linked to the Trust. The FIR did not name some of the Trust's prominent office-bearers, triggering criticism on social media. Opposition leaders alleged that senior functionaries had been protected. Five reasons behind the resignations Questions raised during the SIT's preliminary probe The Special Investigation Team (SIT), formed to investigate the alleged theft of offerings, reportedly found indications of irregularities in matters related to donations, offerings and temple management. Sources said Champat Rai's role also came under scrutiny. FIR and arrests increased the pressure Based on the SIT's findings, police registered an FIR against eight accused and later arrested them. The arrests intensified the controversy and increased pressure on the Trust. Former driver's name surfaced in the FIR The FIR names Champat Rai's former driver Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu and his nephew Manish. Investigators allege they manipulated temple offerings along with others associated with the temple, making the case more sensitive. Trust wanted an independent investigation According to sources, the Trust believed senior office-bearers stepping down would prevent questions over the fairness of the investigation and allow agencies to carry out the probe independently. Move aimed at protecting the Trust's credibility Sources said the Trust decided that resignations were necessary to ensure the ongoing investigation did not affect the credibility of Ram Mandir, which is visited by millions of devotees. Saints demanded a wider probe into temple-related bodies During the VHP meeting in Haridwar, several saints reportedly demanded that the investigation should not be limited to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. They also called for a probe into the accounts and expenditure of the Ramalaya Trust, founded by late Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati, and the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Construction Committee, which handled temple construction work before the Supreme Court's verdict in the Ram Janmabhoomi case. VHP postponed Ayodhya meeting amid growing controversy Amid growing anger among saints over the alleged theft of offerings, the VHP postponed its four-day Central Managing Committee meeting scheduled to begin in Ayodhya on June 26. The meeting was to be held at Karsevakpuram, with representatives from all 44 VHP provinces expected to attend. Trust issued clarification on Kagbhushundi idol and silver bricks The controversy widened after allegations surfaced that a donated Kagbhushundi idol and silver bricks had gone missing. On June 24, Akhilesh Yadav claimed on social media that the donated Kagbhushundi idol had disappeared and questioned repeated reports of theft involving temple donations. On Friday, Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut questioned the whereabouts of four kilograms of silver donated by Uddhav Thackeray for Ram Mandir and demanded accountability. The Trust later released photographs stating that the Kagbhushundi idol is kept safely at Karsevakpuram, while the silver bricks remain secure in bank lockers. VHP opposes dissolving the Ram Mandir Trust VHP International Working President Alok Kumar said there is no need to dissolve the Ram Mandir Trust or constitute a new committee. He said the allegations are against certain individuals and not against the Trust as an institution. 'Focus should be on transparency and better management' Alok Kumar said the priority should be to strengthen the temple's management through modern technology, improved monitoring systems and greater transparency. Responding to questions over the SIT investigation, he said the FIR names eight accused but also refers to "others", indicating that the investigation will not be limited to those already named. He said all those found responsible would face a fair and comprehensive investigation.

stories.title: Pooja Pal takes over as BJP state vice president:Party's membership rules come under spotlight; what SP's 7 rebels got?
stories.summary: The BJP's appointment of MLA Pooja Pal as its Uttar Pradesh vice-president has triggered questions over whether the party relaxed its own organisational rules. Expelled from the SP on 14 August, 2025, Pooja was elevated to the key post just 10 months and 12 days later, even though no public record or photograph of her formally joining the BJP has surfaced. According to the BJP constitution, only an 'active member' can hold an organisational post. To qualify as an active member, a person must enroll at least 100 general members. Despite this requirement, Pooja Pal was directly appointed to the state organization. Pooja Pal is currently an attached MLA in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, meaning she is technically an independent legislator. When asked by Dainik Bhaskar whether she had joined the BJP, she replied, ‘I have become a member of the BJP,’ but did not clarify when or where she took the party's membership. Pooja's 'parachute entry' into BJP organisation Becoming a BJP state office-bearer typically requires years of grassroots work through the party's Mandal, district and regional units. One example is Neeraj Singh, son of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who worked for over a decade in the BJP organisation in Lucknow before being appointed State Vice President. In contrast, Pooja Pal was made State Vice President less than 11 months after her expulsion from the SP. Sources said she was also being considered for a ministerial berth during the Yogi government's Cabinet expansion, but the BJP's national leadership ultimately decided against it. No precise answer on when she took membership We spoke to Kaushambi BJP District President Dharamraj Maurya regarding Pooja Pal's membership. He says, Pooja Pal has not become a BJP member from Kaushambi. She must have become a member at the state office level; only the state headquarters can tell about this. In Lucknow, BJP's chief spokesperson Dinesh Pratap Singh says, Pooja Pal is a member of the BJP, which is why she has been made an office bearer. Sometimes photos of joining are released, and sometimes they are not. BJP sending 2 big political messages 1. To make her a face suffering from SP's 'mafia rule' Pooja Pal is the biggest and living example of being a victim of the alleged 'goonda raj' (rule of hooligans) of SP in UP politics. On 25 January, 2005, just 10 days after their marriage, her husband and then-MLA Raju Pal were murdered by the henchmen of Atiq Ahmed. Subsequently, on 24 February, 2023, her maternal cousin Umesh Pal was also publicly murdered. In the assembly elections, BJP will put Pooja Pal forward to remind the public how SP-backed mafias harassed a woman. 2. Focus on UP's 'Pal' vote bank The Pal community has a large vote bank in Uttar Pradesh, which opposition parties have also put all their efforts into wooing. Currently, Shyam Lal Pal is the state president of SP, and Vishwanath Pal is the state president of BSP. To break this encirclement by the opposition, BJP has made these moves- In the Rajya Sabha elections 2024, a total of 7 Samajwadi Party MLAs rebelled by cross-voting. However, not everyone's luck was the same when it came to receiving rewards.

stories.title: Electricity becomes cheaper across UP from July:Power tariff reduced by 16 paise per unit after regulator's intervention
stories.summary: Lakhs of electricity consumers in Uttar Pradesh will see lower power bills from July after the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) reduced the Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) by 16 paise per unit, making electricity 4.43% cheaper. The revised FPPCA rates were issued by UPPCL on Monday evening following directions from the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC). The reduction marks the largest relief in the past 15 months. Previously, electricity tariffs had been reduced by 2.42% in March 2026. The latest decision is expected to save consumers across the state ₹358.31 crore. Why have electricity rates been reduced? Under the annual tariff order, UPERC had fixed the average power procurement cost at ₹4.94 per unit. However, power distribution companies purchased electricity in April 2026 at an average cost of ₹4.78 per unit, resulting in a saving of 16 paise per unit. The benefit of this lower procurement cost is now being passed on to consumers through reduced electricity bills in July. Regulator stops incorrect fuel surcharge calculation The reduction follows UPERC's intervention after electricity companies allegedly imposed an incorrect 10% FPPCA in June through faulty calculations. The Consumer Council challenged the surcharge before the regulatory commission, following which UPERC issued a strict order on June 23, 2026. The commission directed power companies to calculate FPPCA solely on the basis of the actual monthly power purchase cost and transmission charges, and prohibited them from including liabilities or losses from previous months. Consumer body alleges ₹2,000 crore excess recovery According to the Consumer Council, electricity companies have overcharged consumers by nearly ₹2,000 crore over the past 14 months by using incorrect FPPCA calculations. A separate petition has been filed before UPERC seeking a refund of the allegedly excess amount recovered from consumers. How the alleged overcharging happened Power companies calculate FPPCA every month and adjust it in electricity bills after a specified gap. For example, the variation in power purchase cost for March is reflected in the July bill. However, while imposing the 10% FPPCA in June, companies allegedly added not only the price difference for electricity purchased in February but also outstanding dues worth ₹1,400 crore, which should not have been included. According to the Consumer Council, this resulted in the recovery of ₹2,801 crore instead of the permissible ₹684 crore. July bills to reflect only actual cost difference Power companies were reportedly planning to continue charging 10% FPPCA in July as well. Following the regulatory commission's order, however, they will now be allowed to recover only the actual difference in power purchase cost. UPERC has directed that FPPCA from July onwards must be calculated strictly in accordance with the prescribed formula. What is FPPCA? Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) is an additional charge included in electricity bills to compensate power distribution companies when the cost of fuel used for power generation or the cost of purchasing electricity increases. According to the power department, fuel surcharges are imposed to recover such additional expenses. Rising fuel prices, partly driven by the Middle East crisis, had increased electricity generation and procurement costs, leading to higher fuel surcharge charges in recent months. Energy Minister had also expressed displeasure Energy minister had earlier objected The issue had also drawn criticism from Uttar Pradesh's Energy Minister. On June 11, the minister wrote to UPPCL Chairman Ashish Goyal, expressing strong displeasure over the decision to increase the fuel surcharge by 10% without informing him. In his letter, the minister described the decision as "irresponsible" and accused officials of taking steps that were damaging the government's image. He said such a major decision was implemented without his approval or prior intimation, triggering widespread criticism of the government in the media and on social media.

stories.title: Lucknow becomes India's largest BrahMos production hub:Missile output increases by 20%, first batch completed
stories.summary: With the launch of the new BrahMos Aerospace mega manufacturing facility in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India's BrahMos missile production capacity has increased by nearly 20 percent. The facility has now become the largest BrahMos production centre in the country. Speaking to an international news agency, BrahMos Aerospace Co-Director Alexander Maksichev said the first batch of BrahMos missiles has already been completed at the Lucknow facility, while production of the second batch is currently underway. Production speed and capacity receive major boost Maksichev said the commissioning of the new production centre has significantly enhanced both the speed and capacity of BrahMos missile manufacturing. The expanded capability will enable India to meet the operational requirements of its armed forces more quickly and efficiently. Four BrahMos manufacturing units now operational According to BrahMos Aerospace, four BrahMos production facilities are currently operational across India. Among them, the newly inaugurated Lucknow mega facility is the largest, marking a significant milestone in the country's defence manufacturing sector. Lucknow emerging as a major defence manufacturing hub The BrahMos production centre is regarded as one of the flagship projects of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor. Besides strengthening India's strategic defence capabilities, the facility is expected to generate local employment, boost defence manufacturing, and promote the development of advanced technologies in the region.

stories.title: Trainer aircraft crashes on Kasganj highway in UP:Wobbles at 50 feet, hits power lines before crashing
stories.summary: A trainee aircraft crashed near a six-lane highway behind the police lines in Kasganj on Monday, leaving a woman trainee pilot injured. According to initial reports, the aircraft became entangled in overhead power lines during the flight before crashing near the highway. Pilot shifted to Agra for advanced treatment Local residents and emergency response teams rushed to the accident site immediately after the crash. The injured trainee pilot was given first aid before being referred to a hospital in Agra for advanced medical treatment. Her condition has not yet been officially disclosed. Investigation underway Police and administrative officials reached the scene soon after receiving information about the accident. A large crowd gathered at the crash site as authorities secured the area. Officials have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the crash. Further details are awaited.

stories.title: Fortuner driver threatens traffic cop after Kanpur road accident:Man claims, 'MP Bhole Singh is my uncle, I'll call him right now'
stories.summary: A group of allegedly intoxicated men travelling in a Toyota Fortuner allegedly hit a motorcyclist in Kanpur on Sunday night, assaulted him after he protested, and threatened a traffic policeman who attempted to intervene and record the incident. The accused allegedly invoked the name of BJP MP Devendra Singh alias Bhole Singh, claiming, "Do you know MP Bhole Singh? He's my uncle. I'll call him right now." The incident took place at Green Park Crossing on VIP Road. A video of the confrontation has now surfaced. Fortuner hits motorcyclist According to eyewitnesses, the white Toyota Fortuner (registration number UP 78 HV 6007) was travelling from the DG College side with four to five occupants inside. As the SUV reached the turn near Green Park Crossing on VIP Road, it allegedly collided with a motorcycle, throwing the rider onto the road. Instead of resolving the matter, the occupants reportedly got out of the vehicle, argued with the biker, and physically assaulted him. They also allegedly tried to force him into their vehicle. 2 pictures of hooliganism on the road Policeman threatened while recording video Hearing the commotion, bystanders and a traffic policeman rushed to the spot and rescued the biker. As the situation escalated, the traffic constable began recording the incident on his mobile phone while simultaneously calling for backup over the police wireless network. He was heard saying, "Sir, please send additional force immediately. These people are creating a disturbance, misbehaving, assaulting him, and trying to take him away in their vehicle." The accused then confronted the policeman, saying, "You really enjoy making videos. What's your name?" The constable calmly replied, "It's written on my nameplate. Read it." Before additional police personnel could arrive, the accused fled the scene in their SUV, heading towards Phoolbagh. Police register case Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central), Atul Kumar Srivastava, said a video of the incident, which occurred on June 28, had come to light. He said that although no victim has formally approached the police so far, the police have registered a case on their own. Authorities are now identifying those involved and action will be taken against the accused. Who is Devendra Singh alias Bhole Singh? Devendra Singh, popularly known as Bhole Singh, is a senior BJP leader and the Member of Parliament from the Akbarpur Lok Sabha constituency in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur Dehat district. Born on April 2, 1954, in Madhavapur village of Auraiya district, he was elected MLA from Derapur Assembly constituency in 1991 and 1996 and later served as a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government. He has represented the Akbarpur Lok Sabha seat for three consecutive terms, winning the 2014, 2019, and 2024 general elections. He has also served on parliamentary committees related to energy, agriculture, and rural development.

stories.title: Jaipur hot water assault case reaches UP:State organisations seek CM Yogi's intervention; victim says line duty isn't justice
stories.summary: The case of Reshu Gupta, the Jaipur momos vendor who suffered severe burn injuries after a police constable allegedly threw boiling water on her while clearing the route for the Chief Minister's convoy, has now reached Uttar Pradesh. Several organisations in Uttar Pradesh have written to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the National Commission for Women (NCW) and the Uttar Pradesh State Women's Commission, seeking the victim's protection, rehabilitation and dignified livelihood. While the Rajasthan government has announced that it will bear the cost of her treatment, provide financial assistance and allot a dairy booth to help rehabilitate the family, Reshu said the measures do not amount to justice. "Placing the constable on line duty is not justice for me," she said. Reshu, a native of Ambedkar Nagar district in Uttar Pradesh, moved to Jaipur with her sister after their father's death in 2020 to earn a living. On June 22, her sister lodged an FIR at Ramnagaria police station. UP organisations seek rehabilitation The Rehri-Patri Operators National Organisation, based in Uttar Pradesh, has urged the Chief Minister, the NCW and the Uttar Pradesh State Women's Commission to intervene in the case. In its representation, the organisation's National President, Shyam Kishore Gupta, said Reshu became the family's sole breadwinner after her father's death and that the incident would have long-term consequences for her livelihood. The organisation has urged the women's commissions to take suo motu cognisance of the incident and ensure the victim's security, rehabilitation and financial assistance. Appeal for vending space The organisation has also reuested the Uttar Pradesh government to allot Reshu a vending space in a developed vending zone in a major city so she can rebuild her livelihood in a safe environment. It further urged the state government to expand organised vending zones to reduce the migration of street vendors and unemployed youth to other states. Organisation offers interim support Shyam Kishore Gupta said that if government assistance is delayed, the organisation will try to provide Reshu space for a shop or cart in one of the Pink Vending Zones operating in Uttar Pradesh. He added that a delegation would soon visit Jaipur to meet Reshu and her sister, Khushboo, and extend legal and financial support. 'Half of my body has been burnt' The Rajasthan Police has placed the accused constable, Narendra, on line duty pending departmental action. Responding to the relief announced by the Rajasthan government, Reshu said, "Half of my body has been burnt. These announcements are not justice for me."

stories.title: GDA cancels tenders of Kalyan Mandapam operators:Authority now doing bookings itself; halls may be available at cheaper rates
stories.summary: The Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA) has cancelled the tenders given for the operation of Kalyan Mandapams. Now the authority is doing the bookings itself. On Sunday, the first booking event was also completed at the Kalyan Mandapam located in Bichhiya. The authority's rationale behind taking the operation responsibility into its own hands is that this will enable people to get venues for auspicious events at lower costs. Following the instructions of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, GDA and the Municipal Corporation have constructed several Kalyan Mandapams in the city. The objective was that people should not have to spend huge amounts of money for organizing auspicious events. They should get venues at affordable rates where they can organize their events. However, after the inauguration of the Kalyan Mandapams, the responsibility of their operation was given to private firms. GDA has built Kalyan Mandapams in Manbela, Mohripur and Bichhiya in the city. Among these, operation rights were given for Manbela and Mohripur, which were cancelled a few days ago. Know at what price the authority will do the booking GDA has fixed two rates for booking. One is ₹21 thousand, and the other rate is ₹11 thousand. Booking at ₹11 thousand will be only for Antyodaya card holders. Common people can book at ₹21 thousand. The booking for the event held on Sunday in Bichhiya was done at ₹21 thousand only. Can make separate arrangements for decoration Only hall booking will be done by the authority. This will also include the front open space. Besides, if those making the booking want a stage, lighting, or other decorations, they can get it done at their own discretion. They can discuss this with tent houses or caterers of their choice. Even with decorations, their work will be done in ₹80 to ₹85 thousand. Operation being conducted by Municipal Corporation The Municipal Corporation is getting operations conducted through private firms. However, bookings there are also being done at prescribed rates only. After that, if any other facility is needed, the operator is providing it by charging separately. Doing bookings themselves for people's convenience GDA Vice Chairman Abhinav Gopal said that the authority is doing bookings itself for people's convenience. People will have to pay very low rent. Bookings are being done for ₹11 thousand for Antyodaya card holders and ₹21 thousand for general people. This booking has started in the authority. People should not fall into the trap of any middlemen. They can come directly to the authority office and get their booking done. Booking will be done on a first-come, first-served basis.

stories.title: All eight accused sent to 14-day judicial custody:Police question Champat Rai in Ram Mandir theft case
stories.summary: In the ongoing controversy over the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, all eight accused were produced before a court on Monday. Police did not seek their custodial remand, following which the court sent them to 14 days of judicial custody. The next hearing has been scheduled for July 13, and all eight accused will remain in jail until then. Former trust members questioned Former office-bearers Champat Rai, Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao were questioned in connection with the alleged donation theft case at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. Investigators recorded their statements as part of the ongoing probe. Following the questioning, Champat Rai left for Delhi. Meanwhile, the matter has reached the Supreme Court. The apex court declined an urgent hearing on advocate Anoop Awasthi's petition seeking a CBI investigation into the alleged theft. Questioning the urgency, the court remarked, "What is the urgency?" and said the matter would be heard only after the court's vacation. Police Scrutinise Bank Accounts of Eight Accused On Monday morning, at around 10:30 am, Ayodhya police visited the SBI Ayodhya Dham branch to examine the bank accounts of the eight accused currently lodged in jail. Seven of the accused hold accounts at the same branch. Police collected their bank statements and will now investigate how much money was deposited into their accounts after they began working at the Ram Temple. Notices have also been served to two SBI employees as part of the investigation. 2 photos- SIT submitted its report on June 23, followed by arrests 2 days later The theft case was first reported on June 7. The Uttar Pradesh government formed an SIT on June 13. The SIT submitted its report to Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad on June 23. On June 25, an FIR was registered on the complaint of Trust member Krishna Mohan, naming eight individuals, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu. However, senior officials such as Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra were not named in the FIR. Within hours of the FIR being filed, police arrested all eight accused, including Tinnu. On June 26, a CJM court sent all the accused to jail for three days. On the same day, Ram Mandir Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr. Anil Mishra resigned. The next day, the Trust stated that the matter would be decided in the meeting scheduled for July 11.

stories.title: Akhilesh's son and daughter offer prayers at Kashi Vishwanath:SP chief's children and MP Priya Saroj enjoy Ganga river cruise
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s son Arjun and daughter Tina visited Varanasi on Sunday evening. They were accompanied by Samajwadi Party MP from Machhlishahr, Priya Saroj. The trio first offered prayers at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. They later visited the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple and performed rituals. Afterward, they toured the Ganga ghats by boat and enjoyed a river cruise for about an hour. During the visit, Tina was seen making reels. The Kashi visit of Arjun and Tina, who are twin siblings, was reportedly kept completely confidential. See 3 pictures... Arjun-Tina First Had Darshan of Baba Vishwanath On Sunday evening around 6 PM, SP chief's son Arjun Yadav and daughter Tina Yadav arrived in Kashi. They stayed at a hotel here. From the hotel, the brother-sister duo reached Kashi Vishwanath Temple along with SP MP from Machhlishahr Priya Saroj and former municipal president Vishnu Sharma "Vishwakarma". Here, the brother and sister performed puja and worship. They performed abhishek with milk and Holy Ganga River water. They also worshipped other deities installed in the temple premises. During this time, SP supporters got the information. As soon as they received the news, a large number of SP workers and supporters reached outside the temple premises. The crowd of supporters increased. To control the crowd and maintain security arrangements, the police administration became alert. Police personnel took the brother-sister in a security cordon and brought them out of the temple premises. After this, Arjun and Tina reached Sankat Mochan Temple. Here, they performed puja and worship with proper rituals. The police administration remained vigilant throughout the entire program. After offering prayers, media personnel attempted to speak with both of them. However, neither gave any statement. After temple darshan, they toured by boat After offering prayers, Arjun and Tina had darshan of Mother Ganga. Then, they sat in a boat and toured the ghats of Kashi. Both took selfies during this time. Both stayed at the temple and the Ganga ghat for about an hour. After this, both returned. Before this, both went to Manish Yadav's sweet shop, where both ate Banarasi peda and rasgulla.

stories.title: UP govt hikes pension by ₹500 for widows, elderly, specially-abled:Know the benefits of 8 major pension schemes and free housing eligibility
stories.summary: The UP government is running several pension schemes for the elderly, widows, and disabled persons in the state. Additionally, financial assistance is provided for farmers under the Chief Minister Farmer Accident Welfare Scheme and for women victims of triple talaq and acid attacks. How much pension is provided under these schemes? Who are eligible for this? What is the application process? Know in this report Old age pension Government increased pension, ₹18 thousand will be received annually In UP, economically weaker elderly persons aged 60 years or above will receive ₹18 thousand annually. The state government has increased the old age pension from ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 per month. An installment of ₹4,500 is sent to the beneficiary's bank account every third month. According to the government's new directive, Aadhaar card will no longer be accepted as age proof for applications. Senior citizens will have to show their high school marksheet or family register to prove their age. If senior citizens in urban areas do not have a family register, they can submit photocopies of voter ID, ration card, driving license, passport, or PAN card. Along with this, they also need to provide a self-declaration. Senior citizens availing this pension should not be receiving benefits from other government pension schemes. They should not be retired government employees. The annual family income should not exceed ₹46 thousand 80 in rural areas and ₹56 thousand 460 in urban areas. For any information, you can call the Social Welfare Department's toll-free number 1800-419-0001. Widow pension Widows will now get a house along with pension In UP, women struggling with financial hardship after their husband's death can avail the benefits of the 'Widow Pension Scheme'. Under this, women will now receive ₹1,500 every month. Earlier ₹1,000 was given. These women will also be linked to Ayushman Bharat, Jan Arogya Yojana, PM Awas Yojana and CM Awas Yojana. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath himself announced this on June 15. Only women aged 18 years or above can apply for this scheme. The annual family income should not exceed ₹2 lakh. If a woman has remarried or is already receiving benefits from any other government pension scheme, she will not be eligible for this scheme. Divyang and Leprosy pension scheme Assistance of ₹9 thousand every month for persons with disabilities In UP, the 'Divyang and Leprosy Pension Scheme' is running for disabled persons and leprosy patients. Under this, those with 40% or more disability receive assistance of ₹1,000 every month. An installment of ₹3,000 is sent to the beneficiary's account every three months. For disability pension, the applicant's age should be 18 years or more. The annual family income should not exceed ₹46 thousand 80 for rural areas and 56 thousand ₹460 for urban areas. This pension is being given to 11 lakh disabled persons in UP. Meanwhile, people who have become disabled due to leprosy are sent a pension of ₹3,000 per month to their bank accounts. More than 13 thousand people in UP are receiving this pension. Know the eligibility for Divyang and Leprosy pension Selection of eligible beneficiaries is done based on the Disability Certificate issued by the CMO. A person who is already receiving old age, widow, or any other government pension will not be eligible for this scheme. There is no minimum age limit for leprosy patients. Registered disabled persons under this scheme get free travel in UP Roadways buses, tricycles, and other medical equipment benefits. Special scholarships are also given to disabled students. Plan for acid attack survivors - Triple Talaq Victims Divorce victims receive ₹500 every month In UP, pension is given to Muslim women victims of triple talaq and acid attack survivors. The state government provides financial assistance of ₹500 per month, totaling ₹6,000 per year to divorced women. Acid attack survivors are provided assistance according to their condition. Severely affected women can be included in the disabled category. They are given the benefit of the disabled pension scheme. On June 8, 2026, CM Yogi has also announced connecting these women with housing and health facilities. Under this, free housing and free treatment up to ₹5 lakh is being provided. Victims are being given benefits of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Mukhyamantri Awas Yojana and Ayushman Bharat Yojana-Mukhyamantri Jan Arogya Yojana. Chief Minister farmer accident welfare scheme Government assistance on death due to lightning strike, electric shock, fire, snake bite Farmers who lose their lives during farming or in any accident are given benefits under the 'Chief Minister Farmer Accident Welfare Scheme'. Seriously injured farmers are also included in this plan. The government bears the treatment expenses. In case of death, assistance of ₹5 lakh is provided. Under this scheme, the farmer does not have to pay any premium. Even in case of loss of ability of both hands, both legs or both eyes, ₹5 lakh are given. In case of lesser disability, assistance of ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh is provided. The scheme also includes incidents like lightning strike, electric shock, flood, fire, snake or wild animal attack, agricultural machinery accident and murder-robbery. The farmer's age should be between 18 to 70 years. Now the benefit of this scheme is also being given to sharecropper farmers and landless agricultural laborers. It is necessary to apply at the tehsil within 6 months of the accident. Pension for Democracy Warriors Getting ₹20 thousand every month The UP government provides a monthly pension of ₹20 thousand to democracy fighters who were jailed during the Emergency. Along with this, they also receive facilities like free bus travel and cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh. In the state, this facility is being provided under the 'UP Loktantra Senani Samman Yojana' (UP Democracy Fighter Honor Scheme). If a democracy fighter passes away, this amount continues to be given to their husband or wife. For this, the application and verification process is completed at the district administration level. This scheme benefits those people who were sent to jail under the MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act) or DIR (Defence of India Rules) laws during the Emergency imposed between June 25, 1975 and March 21, 1977. 2 Major Central Pension Schemes Implemented in UP Two major pension schemes of the central government are also implemented in UP, which provide financial assistance to the helpless and needy. These include Atal Pension Yojana (APY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan Yojana (PM-SYM) as the main ones. In Atal Pension Yojana, any person between 18 to 40 years can invest and receive a monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after the age of 60 years. Similarly, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan Yojana is for workers in the unorganized sector, which has a provision of ₹3,000 monthly pension after the age of 60 years.

stories.title: Fire breaks out on 21st-floor of Noida's high-rise society:Accident occurred due to AC explosion; spreads across 3 flats, no casualties reported
stories.summary: A major fire broke out on Monday morning at around 8:30 a.m. on the 21st floor of a building in Noida after an air conditioner (AC) explosion. The incident occurred in Aranya Society, a 24-storey residential building in Sector-119. The fire spread rapidly, engulfing three nearby flats within moments. Flames were seen leaping out of windows, while thick smoke filled the entire floor. Panic spread through the building as residents rushed to escape, many running down the stairs in fear for their lives. People from a neighbouring building also tried to douse the flames by spraying water using pipes. Meanwhile, the fire department was immediately informed, and six fire tenders were rushed to the spot. Firefighting operations were launched, and efforts were made to evacuate the building. So far, no casualties have been reported. 3 pictures- What preparations exist for firefighting in high-rise buildings in Noida? In Noida, the Fire Department is equipped with hydraulic platforms and articulating water tower vehicles to deal with fires in high-rise buildings and multi-storey societies. These machines, ranging from 30 to 42 metres in height, can be used to extinguish fires up to around the 10th floor. New 72-metre and 102-metre hydraulic vehicles are also being procured, but have not yet been inducted into service. Supernova in Sector-94 is the tallest building in Noida, planned to be 80 storeys high, with around 60 floors already completed and occupied. At present, only four hydraulic fire vehicles are available there, capable of reaching up to 42 metres. An air-compressed foam system was recently tested at Supernova, which is capable of reaching up to 300 metres for firefighting. However, this system is not yet operational for regular use.

stories.title: MBBS student suicide note mentions, 'Don't blame the girl':Was studying at BHU; took an overdose of anaesthesia in hostel
stories.summary: MBBS student Ritvik Kundu (26) committed suicide in Varanasi. At 10 PM on Sunday, Ritvik took an overdose of medicine at Sushrut Hostel of Kashi Hindu University. When senior students called him, there was no response. Concerned, they reached Ritvik's room. When there was no answer to their calls, they contacted the university's Proctorial Office and police. When the door was opened, Ritvik was found lying on the floor. A medicine drip was attached to his hand. When police searched the room, a 3-page suicide note was found. The forensic team also collected evidence. The suicide note read: I was the apple of my family's eye. Perhaps many people like me will not give up in life. But I am giving up. I apologize to all those whose hearts I have hurt. That girl should not be blamed. She is very good. She loved me a lot. She did so much for me. Take care of her. Police say that the initial investigation suggests the cause of death appears to be an overdose of anesthesia medication. The exact cause will be known after the post-mortem. Dr. Ritwik was posted in the anesthesia department. He was studying in MBBS First Year. He was a resident of Hooghly, West Bengal. The incident is from the Lanka police station area. Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- What was written in the suicide note? Read Ritvik wrote- Please take care of my parents too. I was their biggest hope. But, I could not live up to their expectations. Life goes on. Perhaps this news will break my mother. She loves me the most. Take care of my father and sister too. I was the apple of their eyes. He wrote, 'As I am writing this, I don't know whether I should change my decision or not. Perhaps I don't want to die, but still I will do this. I am perhaps the most selfish person. Not worthy of living on this earth. It may be that people like me are born only to cause pain to others.' Ritvik wrote- Mother, Father and Sister, please forgive me. I wish I could hear your voice one last time. Everyone, take care of yourselves. Throughout my life, I kept running away from reality. Today I am running away forever. Nothing in this world is permanent. I now understand that I will never be able to live that life. Which I had dreamed of. He said, 'We all dream of a completely happy life. But, perhaps this is not possible for anyone. Life is very short. Don't make it shorter by laughing at others' sorrows. Be kind to everyone and be grateful for what you have. World, goodbye.' Students living in nearby rooms being questioned Lanka Police Station In-charge Rajkumar Verma said - Upon receiving information from the Proctorial Board, the in-charge of Nagwan outpost was sent to the spot. A suicide note was found in the room, the contents of which will be investigated. For now, the body has been taken into custody and kept in the mortuary. The family members have been informed. Students living in nearby rooms have been questioned.

stories.title: Storm and rain in 15 cities of UP, waterlogged underpass:Cars, bikes get stranded; 2 killed in lightning strikes, monsoon likely to enter within 24 hrs
stories.summary: A monsoon-triggering weather system has become active in Uttar Pradesh, paving the way for the arrival of the monsoon in the state. On Monday morning, heavy rainfall was recorded in around 15 cities, including Lucknow, Ayodhya, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Badaun, Maharajganj, Deoria, Kushinagar, and Siddharthnagar. In Mirzapur, so much rain fell that up to 3 feet of water accumulated in an underpass, trapping cars and motorcycles. In Basti and Maharajganj, lightning strikes claimed the lives of a woman and a 9-year-old child. Since morning, most parts of the state have been cloudy, with occasional light sunshine in some areas. An alert has been issued for thunderstorms, rain, and lightning in 46 districts today, while a heatwave warning remains in effect for 26 districts. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the monsoon, stalled near the UP–Bihar border for the past 16 days, may enter Uttar Pradesh within the next 24 hours. According to the IMD, the southwest monsoon will enter the state via eastern Uttar Pradesh. This may lead to intense rainfall in the Terai regions, including Kushinagar, Maharajganj, and Siddharthnagar. Normally, the monsoon arrives in Uttar Pradesh by around June 20, but this year it is running about 9–10 days late. New spell of rain from June 30 Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from the Lucknow Meteorological Centre said: Due to increased pre-monsoon activity in the state, temperatures have started to drop. The heatwave is now limited to a few cities and is expected to end within 24 hours. After this, a new spell of rainfall will begin in the state from June 30. Conditions are favorable for the southwest monsoon to advance rapidly, which may lead to a temperature drop of 5–7°C in the first week of July. Weather forecast for the next 3 days in UP: June 30: Light rain is expected in western UP, while eastern UP may see heavy rain with thunderstorms. July 1: Western UP will experience rain with thunder, while eastern UP may receive heavy rainfall. July 2: Heavy rain is expected across the entire state, with winds blowing at speeds of 40–50 km/h.

stories.title: Man who charged ₹100 for certificates became 'Bottle Baba':Some followers still believed, even after the arrest, that his 'holy water' cured illnesses
stories.summary: Kanpur's godman 'Bottle Baba' has come under the spotlight after being accused of performing obscene acts while allegedly treating a woman inside a closed room. Despite the allegations, many of his followers continue to stand by him, claiming he could turn ordinary water into "nectar" with a touch and that drinking it cured various ailments. Bottle Baba's real name is Hariom Yadav. Until about a decade ago, he worked at the Kanpur Dehat tehsil, where he processed income and caste certificates. Villagers say he would charge an extra ₹100- ₹150 on top of the official fee for the service. According to locals, Hariom later reappeared dressed in saffron robes, claiming that Goddess Kali had appeared in his dream and instructed him to help devotees and improve their lives. He then built a Kali Mata temple in his village and began calling himself Hari Dham Sarkar. A regular gathering of devotees was held at the temple, where he would blow over water and ask people to drink it, claiming it had healing powers. On June 19, police arrested Hariom Yadav in connection with a molestation case involving a female follower. He is currently in jail, and his ashrams have been shut down. How Hariom became Baba by claiming Kali's command in a dream? Father was a farmer; he himself used to get income-caste certificates made Chain ka Purwa village is about 33 km away from Kanpur Dehat district headquarters. Talking to the people here, it became clear that one section of the village considers Baba a fraud. While many people call him miraculous. According to the villagers, Hariom's father used to do farming. Hariom was not good at studies. He used to help his father with farming at home. After that, he started working on making income-caste certificates at the tehsil of Kanpur Dehat. He used to earn ₹500-₹600 per day. According to villagers, the turning point came in 2015. One day, Hariom gathered people at the village chaupal and claimed that Goddess Kali had appeared in his dream the previous night. He told them she had instructed him to fulfill the purpose for which he was born. Soon after, a new Kali Mata temple was built in the village, where Hariom began conducting religious rituals. He started hearing devotees' grievances and claimed he could solve their problems. Over the next two years, his following grew rapidly, and by 2017, he had become well-known across the surrounding villages. Here, he claimed to cure people in 3 ways- Gradually, people started coming from distant villages. Around the place where Kali Maa's temple is located, Hariom got an ashram built. He started calling the established deity 'Chain Ki Purwa Wali Devi'. He would often have chants of this name raised in his court. Built an ashram on 8 bighas, started holding court here On August 8, 2022, Hariom organized a big event in the village. To inaugurate the ashram, he called Bharat Das Maharaj of Hanumangarhi, Shyam Narayan, President of Jannayak Karpuri Sena, and retired Allahabad High Court Judge Justice Dr. I.M. Qudusi. This ashram was built on the land of the village's Puttilal Yadav. After building the ashram, Hariom started holding court every Tuesday and Saturday. He would sit on a throne in front of people. Sometimes he would wear groom's clothes, and sometimes he would come in dhoti-kurta. Initially, he would issue a receipt for ₹100. One had to buy a water bottle for ₹20 from the ashram shop. Hariom would claim to turn this water into nectar by touching it. If any follower said they didn't benefit, he would say that you are under a shadow. Special worship would need to be performed. People living with Hariom would write down the worship materials, and these had to be purchased from the ashram itself. The cost of materials would be between ₹3 and ₹5 thousand. Village people say that the receipt that cost ₹100 in 2024 has now become ₹250. In the ashram itself, Hariom Yadav's picture was made with the name Haridham Sarkar. It was sold by showing him as God. Often devotees would take these photo frames and put them up in their homes. Bottle Baba claimed to bring the dead back to life These days, a video of Hariom Baba is going viral. In it, he claims to bring a dead woman back to life. He says that I am neither a Baba, nor a devotee, nor any tantric. I have no guru, nor do I wear any kanthi mala (prayer beads). This Sun and this Kali Maa (Goddess Kali), they are my gurus. After this, he starts making gestures with his hands like performing magic. Then the woman lying down gets up, and people start chanting in praise. No one has any information about who this man was. A person associated with Hariom's ashram says that one of Hariom's disciples was from Mumbai. He was in the police. His son suddenly died, after which he went there. When he couldn't bring him back to life, he said that he had reached the feet of God. Now, it won't be right to call him back from there. After this, he returned to his ashram. Apart from Goddess Kali, Hariom would sometimes claim Banke Bihari, Sharda Bhavani, or sometimes Balaji as his guru. He would also make people chant slogans. How did Hariom Yadav finally get caught? On June 5th, Hariom reached a woman's house in Auraiya. Her husband was working in Rajasthan. This house was the woman's maternal home. She had also called her in-laws. After performing the havan-puja, Hariom said that the woman was under the shadow of ghosts and spirits. She would have to come to Haridham Ashram. He asked her to come to the darbar on the new moon day on June 15th. The woman reached the ashram on June 15th with her two brothers-in-law. She says that Hariom took her to a room for exorcism and started molesting her there. After that, I ran outside. Hariom also came out. He said that she is under the shadow of ghosts and spirits; she will have to be whipped. Hariom ordered the woman's brothers-in-law and his nephew to whip her. Everyone kept whipping the woman. She kept pleading with folded hands to be released while crying and writhing in pain. This continued for about 30 minutes. After this, the woman reached Bhognipur police station, about 18 kilometers away from the ashram, and told the police the entire incident. Then the woman's medical examination was conducted. A case was registered against Hariom Yadav, his nephew Deepak, disciple Kundan, and both brothers-in-law Ramvir and Sukhvir. The police arrested Hariom Yadav and his nephew. Hariom says- All the allegations are false. Allegations keep being made against Sanatanists. Ashish Dwivedi, a leader from Dibiyapur, is trying to frame me. I don't have any small ashram, it is built on 8 bighas. After presenting in court, he has been sent to jail.

stories.summary: General Secretary Champat Rai left Ayodhya for Delhi on Sunday evening after resigning from the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. He remained at the Ram Temple until around 3 pm before departing. Sources said Champat Rai is likely to attend the Trust meeting scheduled for July 11, where his resignation is expected to be taken up for consideration. He submitted his resignation on Friday. Meanwhile, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is closely monitoring the temple donation theft case. On the instructions of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Eastern Uttar Pradesh regional pracharak Anil Kumar has reached Ayodhya. He has been holding continuous meetings with sadhus, saints, mahants and people associated with the Ram Temple. Sources also said preparations to introduce a new administrative structure in the Ram Temple Trust have gathered pace. A final decision on reconstituting the Trust may be taken after Prime Minister Narendra Modi returns from his overseas visit. Discussions are underway on assigning greater responsibilities to Ayodhya's saints and representatives from various sections of society. The RSS regional pracharak will submit a report to Mohan Bhagwat RSS regional pracharak Anil Kumar, who has been camping in Ayodhya since Saturday (June 27), spent around two hours at the Ram Temple on Saturday evening. He offered prayers to Ram Lalla and also interacted with key temple sevaks. He also held discussions with prominent mahants of Ayodhya regarding the alleged issue of misappropriation of offerings. During these meetings, he spoke with Mahant Maithiliraman Sharan of Lakshman Kila, Dr. Mithileshnandini Sharan of Hanumant Nivas, Mahant Kamalnayan Das, successor of Maniram Das Chhawni, and Mahant Shashikant Das, president of the Saryu Aarti committee, seeking their views. He is expected to continue discussions with saints and mahants in Ayodhya on Monday as well. After completing his interactions, he will compile a detailed report and submit it to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat. Earlier, RSS All India Executive Committee member Bhaiyaji Joshi (Suresh Joshi) had also stayed in Ayodhya for a night and held discussions with saints and mahants associated with the temple. He has already submitted his report to the RSS chief. Ram Mandir's RMO Arjun Dev also on SIT's radar Arjun Dev was responsible for monitoring 1600 cameras A new name has emerged in the investigation of the Ram Temple donation theft case. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has also brought the role of Radio Operation Officer (RMO) Arjun Dev, deployed at Ram Janmabhoomi, under the scope of investigation. Arjun Dev was responsible for monitoring the CCTV cameras installed in the counting room where donations were counted. Besides this, Arjun Dev was also responsible for monitoring approximately 1,600 cameras installed at Ram Janmabhoomi. Now, his role in the surveillance system is being investigated. According to sources, the report also mentions his continuous posting in Ayodhya for 17 years and active interference in the trust's work. RMO Arjun was also handling CCTV work when Ramlalla was in the tent. Arjun Dev appeared arrogantly before SIT The counting of offerings to Ram Lalla in the counting room was monitored by CCTV cameras. The investigating agency is trying to find out how the offerings were stolen despite security arrangements. Why surveillance was not maintained. On this basis, SIT had also questioned Arjun Dev during its initial 3-day investigation. According to sources, when called for questioning, Arjun Dev appeared before the SIT and sat on the chair in a stiff manner. However, instead of answering directly, he said that he would respond through his lawyer. It is being reported that the investigating officers reprimanded him and advised him to maintain the dignity and decorum of his position. Transfer happened many times, but was stopped every time Arjun Dev has been continuously posted in Ayodhya since 2009. During this period, transfer orders were issued several times, but his transfer was stopped every time. Recently, the transfer order issued for Lucknow was also cancelled. Arjun Dev had close relations with some officials of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Due to these connections, his transfers kept getting stopped repeatedly. The SIT is also investigating who was getting the last transfer stopped. Why was the transfer stopped repeatedly? What was the meaning of such a long posting in the same district? Questions also raised on active role in trust's work Apart from CCTV surveillance, Arjun Dev's monitoring also included maintaining wireless communication between police, PAC, CRPF and other security agencies from the control room of the temple premises, staying in contact with personnel on duty, and facilitating immediate exchange of information regarding VIP movement and emergency situations. According to sources, the SIT investigation revealed that Arjun Dev was not limited only to wireless and security-related responsibilities. The investigation has revealed that he also played an active role in several administrative activities of the trust in VIP darshan arrangements. For this reason, questions have also been raised about his working style and activities beyond his jurisdiction. Two years ago, Arjun Dev had stopped the Shankaracharya from darshan About two years ago, Arjun Dev was in the news when he stopped Shankaracharya Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati and his security personnel during the darshan of Ram Lalla. Because the Shankaracharya is associated with the Ram Mandir movement, he wanted to have darshan with his associates and security personnel according to his position and dignity. It is said that citing security reasons, he had allowed only a limited number of people to enter. After this incident, the Shankaracharya returned without darshan in anger. Even at that time, questions were raised about his behavior.
